tests.name: applied_effect_expires_once_with_remove_tag_message

answer.notes: Pack-level evidence only. I read the file in full but did not open the similar files' test bodies, so the superseded/duplicate calls rest on name similarity. The closest overlap is encounter_job_skills.rs (damage, DoT, stun, buff, knockout), which appears to exercise skill effects through a different API. Confirming that would require comparing its assertions to this file's byte-exact packet checks. Nothing was marked removable, given the refusal and byte-exact canary checks. The most likely future candidates, if overlap is confirmed, are damage_cast, healing and lethal_damage against encounter_job_skills.

last_critiques.notes: All nine tests in tests/abilities.rs are marked keep, with covered_by null, and whole_file_removable is false. No removal verdict exists, so no removal needs an equally strong replacement, and the lens is satisfied. The removal list is empty, so it can be handed to a builder as it stands. Score is held to 6 because the keep reasons are weak in places. Several cite overlap without checking it: piece_037 first-aid tests, piece_067 and warpstone cooldown tests, and piece_056 tick_expires_the_row_exactly_once were not read. The damage_cast reason says it was not verified line by line. The auditor's own confidence is 0.5. These gaps only matter if a later audit turns them into removals, which would then need the covering tests opened first. I did not open the comparison files myself, since no removal depends on them.

tests.name: definitions_above_the_player_level_or_of_another_job_are_not_served

answer.notes: The similar-file pack (coin_store_siblings, kart_service, inventory, player_trade, fishing_review) has no ability/cast tests and gives no overlap. Searching the rest of the repo found overlapping coverage in two places: src/abilities.rs `mod tests::unsupported_cast_rejects_the_malformed_20_byte_shape` (unit level, a few cast shapes) and src/gameplay/w64_regional_quest_tests.rs::ability_definition_lookup_and_unsupported_casts_are_explicit (gameplay level, a subset of definition lookups and refused casts). Those overlap in part but neither asserts the full set here, so no test is marked removable. The strongest candidate for a later trim is definitions_above_the_player_level_or_of_another_job_are_not_served, which could be reduced to the level-20/profile-9 checks if the w64 test were extended. No later task superseding these functions was identified; the pack gave no created_by/last_changed_by values for this file.

last_critiques.notes: Every verdict is keep, so no removal needs a replacement and whole_file_removable=false is correct. The two overlap tests the auditor cites both exist: prototype/osfr-tools/src/abilities.rs:981 (unsupported_cast_rejects_the_malformed_20_byte_shape) and prototype/osfr-tools/src/gameplay/w64_regional_quest_tests.rs:2453 (ability_definition_lookup_and_unsupported_casts_are_explicit). The auditor's own reasoning says neither fully covers this file, so keeping all eight is the safe call. Lower confidence in the audit's 0.7 is fair: the auditor did not check the w64 test's assertions line by line, so the claim that it is a subset is unverified. answer.notes: The last three tests and the bodies of the picker and look-alike tests were judged from names, doc lines and the earlier pass, not from a full read of their bodies. The file is dominated by refusal, security, persistence and canary checks. The only partial overlaps are with tests/login.rs (account_login_rejects_a_character_owned_by_another_account, delete_checks_ownership_on_the_file_and_keeps_characters_saved_since, picker_names_pass_check_name_and_create_through_the_login_service, account_name_check_and_create_share_global_uniqueness), and each of those is weaker in scope. Nothing here is a clear duplicate, so no removals are proposed. Lowering confidence to 0.5 because the last three verdicts were not checked against bodies.

problems.issue: Verdict is labelled "superseded" with covered_by login.rs::account_login_rejects_a_character_owned_by_another_account, but the reason text says keep, and the auditor's own notes say it kept it 'in substance'. The label and the reason contradict each other. The cited login test does assert selected_binding.is_none() for a foreign character (login.rs ~line 469), so it covers the bind refusal at the wire/service layer. It does not call select_and_bind_session or AuthenticatedSession directly, and it does not assert the store-level NotOwnedOrMissing status. Delete ownership is covered at service level by login.rs delete_checks_ownership (delete_status 2), but that is not the store-level NotOwnedOrMissing path. This is a security refusal, so the lens requires an equally strong named replacement, and none is established.
problems.fix: keep it. Change the verdict to keep and cite the login.rs pair only as partial overlap, not as a replacement. Do not put it on any removal list.

problems.issue: The keep verdicts cite login.rs as not covering the same path. I could only partly verify this, because the read tool failed on login.rs and account.rs bodies, and search returned only single lines. The moderation test (tests[9]) was judged from its name and body without reading the moderation module, as the auditor admits. These keeps are safe for removal purposes, but the uniqueness claims are unverified.
problems.fix: keep it. No removal depends on these claims. Re-verify only if a later pass proposes removing any of them.

last_critiques.notes: The removal list is effectively empty: every test is kept, and whole_file_removable is false, which is correct. The problem is the contradictory 'superseded' label on a security refusal test. A builder reading the label could remove the only store-level NotOwnedOrMissing check. Fix the label to keep before wiring. Confidence in the keep-all outcome is good. The superseded label is the only defect I found.

problems.issue: accented_and_cased_look_alikes_of_a_saved_name_are_taken is kept on a name-level judgment. The audit says login.rs::split_variants_of_a_taken_name_are_taken is related but 'was not compared in full'. The keep is conservative, not evidenced.
moderation_and_uniqueness_share_the_folded_words was judged from its doc line only, with no body read. The audit's own notes say the last three verdicts were not checked against bodies.
the_longest_names_the_creator_picker_offers_pass_check_name_and_create is kept as 'not a duplicate' based on a summary of login.rs, not on a comparison of bodies.

name_check_and_create_return_client_status_codes and the other keeps cite login.rs as weaker, but the rationale is a summary, not a line-by-line comparison. This is acceptable because no removal depends on it.
session_cannot_bind_another_accounts_character_and_delete_checks_owner is a security refusal. It is kept, which is the correct conservative choice.

last_critiques.notes: No test is marked superseded, duplicate or obsolete, and whole_file_removable is false. The removal list is empty, so no removal verdict needs a covering test, and the security, refusal, persistence and canary tests are all kept. The pass is therefore safe, but the audit is thin. Several keep reasons rest on test names, doc lines or 'not seen elsewhere' rather than on bodies, and the audit's own confidence is 0.5. Before any future removal pass, the builder should re-read login.rs against tests[5], [7] and [8]. The automatic id check was empty and the cross notes are empty, so there is nothing to reconcile.

answer.notes: The pack showed the previous verdicts only for the first six tests, and the remaining tests were not compared against the similar files' assertion bodies. I kept everything except gateway_offer_cancel_restores_state_and_rejects_a_stale_quit, which the pack directly ties to derby_route. The most likely further removals are active_activity_refuses_derby_without_consuming_the_npc_menu (vs derby_route::busy_derby_refusal_keeps_the_exact_menu_for_a_retry) and possibly trade_requests_reach_the_binary_with_gameplay_loaded. Both need an assertion-level read before they are marked duplicate. The file is a broad hostile-input and routing corpus and should not be removed whole.

problems.issue: gateway_offer_cancel_restores_state_and_rejects_a_stale_quit is marked superseded by derby_route.rs::offer_cancel_through_gameplay_restores_the_job_and_keeps_stale_quit_inert, but the covering test is a direct Gameplay::handle_in_world call with no gateway, no wrap/unwrap of the wire, and no nearby broadcast. The gateway test also asserts cancelled.nearby contains a [35,0,7,0] packet, which the covering test never checks. It additionally checks the stale quit through the gateway snapshot. The covering test does not assert at least as much, so the removal is unbacked.

active_activity_refuses_derby_without_consuming_the_npc_menu is marked superseded by derby_route.rs::busy_derby_refusal_keeps_the_exact_menu_for_a_retry, but the two differ in path and activity. The app_fuzz test drives the gateway with a mining activity (fixture.active("mining")) and asserts the whole gateway snapshot is unchanged and that the first and retry replies are non-empty. The covering test uses Gameplay directly with a harvesting job and asserts state equality and derby_active. The gateway routing and the mining-busy case are not exercised by the covering test, so the removal is unbacked.

The auditor's own notes say only about five test bodies were read and the rest were judged by name and doc line, with moderate confidence (0.45). Keep verdicts are reasonable as conservative, but the removal evidence does not meet the lens standard: a removal verdict must rest on a read of the covering body.

last_critiques.notes: The whole-file removable verdict is correctly false and the keep verdicts on the security, refusal, persistence and canary tests are acceptable. Both superseded removals fail the evidence check: the named covering tests exist (derby_route.rs lines 970 and 1011), but neither matches the gateway-level path or the assertions of the file under audit. Since the removal list would drop the only gateway-level nearby and routing checks for these behaviours, the audit should be corrected to keep tests[5] and tests[8] before any builder acts on it.

problems.issue: gateway_offer_cancel_restores_state_and_rejects_a_stale_quit (app_fuzz.rs:1356) is marked superseded by derby_route::offer_cancel_through_gameplay_restores_the_job_and_keeps_stale_quit_inert, but that covering test calls Gameplay::handle_in_world directly and never goes through the routed Gateway. The removed test drives the wrapped gateway and asserts the nearby broadcast [35,0,7,0] and a whole-snapshot equality after the stale quit. The covering test asserts [35,0,20] and only game.state() equality. The gateway routing and the [35,0,7,0] broadcast are not covered elsewhere, so this is not a duplicate. Fix: keep it.

gateway_pending_game_cancel_retires_without_rewards (app_fuzz.rs:1414) is marked superseded, but the cited derby_route::offer_cancel_and_running_quit_retire_without_rewards_and_stale_quit_is_inert (derby_route.rs:653) uses DerbyGateway, not the app gateway. It tests a Running-phase quit, not a pending-game cancel sent with instance+1. The removed test's key check, that a stale cancel leaves the whole snapshot unchanged (assert_eq!(gateway.snapshot(), before)), is not made by the covering test, which only checks the phase. The verdict itself admits the bodies were not compared. Fix: keep it.

active_activity_refuses_derby_without_consuming_the_npc_menu (app_fuzz.rs:1532) is marked superseded by derby_route::busy_derby_refusal_keeps_the_exact_menu_for_a_retry (derby_route.rs:970). The covering test does match the path at gameplay level (state equality and retry), but the removed test runs through the gateway with a snapshot comparison and a 'mining' active activity fixture, so the gateway-level refusal path is lost. The verdict's 'medium confidence' is not backed by a body comparison. Fix: keep it unless the gateway-level refusal is re-covered.

last_critiques.notes: Only three removal verdicts were proposed, and I checked all three against the covering test bodies. None is a true replacement: each covering test is at the gameplay or DerbyGateway layer, while the app_fuzz originals drive the routed Gateway and assert snapshot equality or the nearby broadcast. Those are the security and refusal properties the lens protects. The keep verdicts for the remaining tests are conservative and acceptable. whole_file_removable=false is correct. The file should be kept intact, or the removal list reduced to zero, before it is handed to a builder.

answer.notes: The pack's previous_answer was truncated after the first 11 tests, so the earlier verdicts for the last four tests were not visible. I did not open the repository files or the similar files, so this is based on the pack alone. Most tests here are row-specific analogues of tests/bixie_hive_dungeon.rs. Under the conservative rule I kept them, because the per-row constants, prizes, positions and gates differ. The only real overlap is the GUID walk (partial), which I also kept. If the team wants to cut duplication, the best candidates are the start-screen and second-session tests, which could share a parametrised helper with bixie_hive_dungeon.rs rather than being removed.

problems.issue: Marked duplicate of bixie_hive_dungeon::the_start_screen_carries_the_instance_and_roster_count, but the covering test does not check this row's roster count (DETAILS_ROSTER at 525) or its four-prize preview against this row's data. It also drives a different entry (interact vs open_battle helper) and asserts DETAILS_LEN and the battle id, which this test does not. The bandit version's roster-count and prize-preview assertions are not covered by the bixie test, so removal would drop a per-row check. The auditor's own reason says 'may be kept'.

Marked duplicate of bixie_hive_dungeon::guids_are_unique_across_shipped_content, but the auditor's own reason says it additionally checks field_enemies.json and encounter actors. The bixie test does check field_enemies.json, but the auditor did not confirm encounter-actor coverage there, so the claimed full subset is unverified. The verdict contradicts the reason ('Partial duplicate; ... retain here'). Removing it could drop the encounter-actor GUID collision check.

The auditor did not compare the route, refusal, reload, multi-session and payout tests against bixie_hive_dungeon or thugamug_battle at assertion level (stated in notes). Their keep verdicts are conservative and safe to keep, but the 'not verified as duplicated' reasons are unsupported. No removal is proposed for them.

last_critiques.notes: Only the two 'duplicate' verdicts would remove tests, and neither is backed by a full-strength equivalent. Both should be kept, which makes the whole list a keep-all with no removals. whole_file_removable=false is correct. Confidence 0.5 is consistent with the partial review. A shared parametrised helper is a refactor option, not a removal, and should be a separate task.

problems.issue: Marked duplicate of bixie a_second_session_sees_the_marker_not_the_arena, but the bixie body does not cover the bandit assertions. Bixie checks the second session's entry replies for arena actors and the first player's entry, and never reads the second session's refresh after the first player enters the arena. Bandit (lines 1113-1119) checks that the second stream carries no arena AddNpc after the owner's arena spawn, and (1104-1107) that the owner sees every arena enemy. That aliasing check is absent from bixie, so the bandit test is not a duplicate.

Marked duplicate of the bixie test, but bixie's version only grants coins live. Bandit also grants a filler item between Go and the killing blow and asserts that the item count survives the payout (lines 1171, 1183-1186) and that exactly one prize is added to the live bag (1192-1200). The item-survival invariant is not in bixie's body, so removal would drop a persistence/live-state check.

Verdict superseded is backed, not merely partial. Bixie's guids_are_unique_across_shipped_content (lines 910-985) walks every battle row, including the bandit row once shipped, checks field_enemies.json, checks encounters.json world and dungeon actors and guides, and drives the real EncounterEngine loader. The auditor's keep-unless-extended condition is already met, so removal is supported, but the reason text should be corrected to say so.
problems.fix: remove (reason corrected: bixie test already covers battles, field enemies, encounter actors and loader duplicate refusal)

problems.issue: Duplicate verdict is acceptable. Bixie's test (lines 200-260) checks instance, roster count (5, via DETAILS_ROSTER_COUNT), and all four prize entries against the row. Bandit's version is a per-row constant regression, and the auditor already flags low confidence. Its removal leaves no test of this row's own roster offset, so the removal is backed only by the sibling's use of the same decode path.
problems.fix: remove only if the reviewer accepts losing the per-row roster constant check; otherwise keep it

last_critiques.notes: Verified by reading bodies: guids (superseded, backed), start screen (duplicate, mostly backed), second-session and live-change (both duplicate verdicts are false; bandit checks more than bixie). The auditor's notes say sibling bodies were not re-read, which is why these two verdicts did not hold. Since the pack still rests on two wrong removals, the list is not wireable as it stands. Keep tests[11] and tests[12]. The remaining verdicts (keep ones) were accepted on their stated reasons without line-level re-reads of the bandit file; the refusal, persistence, canary and security tests were not replaced by any named equal test, so they remain kept.

answer.notes: Based on test names, doc lines, the pack's similar-file names, and grep of the tests directory; I did not read the test bodies, so assertion-level overlap is unverified. Most tests are refusal, persistence, canary, or gateway-routed checks that the rules require keeping. Only one candidate is marked superseded (gateway_sc_catalogue_lists_the_ride_and_skips_earn_only vs station_cash.rs::catalogue_packets_carry_the_scaled_price_and_skip_earn_only), and it is low confidence because the gateway route is extra coverage. Candidates for a deeper look: the two buy-back window tests (only_the_ten_most_recent... and buy_back_window_is_bounded_store_data) and the vendor_sell.rs::sale_completion_id_drives_buy_back overlap. No obsolete tests were identified; the T380, T484, F387 and T230 notes describe current behaviour, not replaced behaviour.

problems.issue: Marked superseded by vendor_sell.rs::sale_completion_id_drives_buy_back, claiming the covering test asserts the same restore and this file adds nothing. Checked both bodies: the vendor_sell test does one sell, reads the transaction id, sends one 165/12, and asserts result OK and coins/stack restored. It has no replay check. This file's test (coin_store_siblings.rs:743-775) additionally sends the buy-back three more times and asserts each replay returns RESULT_FAILURE with no charge and the state unchanged. That is a replay-pays-nothing security check the covering test does not make. Removal would lose it.
problems.fix: keep it (or split out the replay loop into a named replacement before removing). The 'adds no further assertion' reason is false.

problems.issue: gateway_sc_wallet_and_ride_order_are_atomic_and_replay_once is marked superseded by station_cash.rs::order_debits_exact_price_and_grants_once, but the auditor's own reason says the overlap is partial and that routing is not confirmed elsewhere. The verdict is not backed: the gateway routing, the atomic insufficient-order refusal and the replay-through-gateway are unverified in station_cash.rs. The covering test was not opened.
problems.fix: keep it unless the covering test is opened and shown to route through the gateway and cover the insufficient-order and replay cases.

problems.issue: gateway_sc_catalogue_lists_the_ride_and_skips_earn_only is marked superseded by station_cash.rs::catalogue_packets_carry_the_scaled_price_and_skip_earn_only without opening either body. The name match is suggestive, but the covering test is not shown to go through the 66/12 gateway route the removed test exercises.
problems.fix: keep it until station_cash.rs:748 is read and shown to drive the same gateway 66/12 path with the same price and earn-only assertions.

problems.issue: About 40 'keep' verdicts are defaults under a conservative rule, not checked against other files. The auditor states it read only two tests and that the file needs a full read. Their coverage is not established, but they are not proposed for removal, so this is a depth gap rather than an unbacked removal.
problems.fix: keep the file. Do a full read before any future removal pass.

last_critiques.notes: whole_file_removable=false is correct. The three superseded removals are not backed: one is contradicted by the covering test body (no replay check there), and two rest on name matches or self-admitted partial overlap. Two of the three also cover replay or refusal behaviour, which the lens says needs an equally strong named replacement. The pack has no cross notes or id-check failures. The list cannot be handed to a builder as it stands: at minimum the three superseded verdicts must be reversed to keep.

problems.issue: Marked superseded by tests/station_cash.rs::catalogue_packets_carry_the_scaled_price_and_skip_earn_only, but the covering test does not assert the scaled price. Its own comment (station_cash.rs:755-757) says the listed price is checked by store_packet_matches_the_client_reader_field_for_field and that it 'only checks the catalogue-level rules'. The removed test asserts SC_RIDE_PRICE is present in the 66/5 store packet, the 66/13 marketplace-enabled reply header and byte, and the routed gateway path (66/12 through Gateway). None of these is driven by the named cover. The audit's own note admits it is conservative and could keep it. The removal is not backed by an equal or stronger named replacement.

Every other verdict is keep, so none is a removal and none can be wrong as a removal. However, the audit states it inspected only the buy-back section and name-matched the rest, and it marks the un-inspected verdicts as provisional. The audit did not verify the sale_completion_id_drives_buy_back (vendor_sell.rs:298) overlap it raised itself. Its keep is therefore not a judgement either way, only a default.

last_critiques.notes: The only removal proposed is gateway_sc_catalogue_lists_the_ride_and_skips_earn_only, and the cited cover does not drive the same routed path or assert the scaled price, so the removal is unbacked. With that fixed to keep, the removal list is empty and whole_file_removable false is correct. The file is 2,178 lines, and the audit's low confidence (0.35) is honest. Whole-file removal is not supported. A future pass that wants to trim should check sale_completion_id_drives_buy_back against the first buy-back test with a full assertion comparison.

answer.notes: All seven tests are kept. The earlier 'superseded' verdict for selling_an_ingredient_back_uses_the_store_price_and_is_once was overturned on reading the body: it asserts the ingredient store resale price, the 165/6 completion layout and remaining==1, and a replayed sell that pays nothing, none of which the cited coin_store_siblings test checks (that test sells a different item from a generic fixture). The refusal tests overlap vendor_sell.rs gateway_vendor_buy_* in path, but they compare full save bytes or malformed bodies that the sibling tests do not, so they are kept. If the suite needs trimming, the insufficient/full-bag section is the candidate, but only after vendor_sell's refusal tests are strengthened to byte-level checks.

problems.issue: selling_an_ingredient_back_uses_the_store_price_and_is_once is marked superseded by coin_store_siblings.rs gateway_sell_then_buy_back_once_then_replays_pay_nothing, but that sibling does not drive the same path. It sells STACK_MANY (item 75060) from a generic Fixture, not a Bordon-bought ingredient at the real 12-coin row, so it never checks the ingredient resale price (resale(2900) against the store row). It also has no sell-replay check: it replays only the 165/12 buy-back, while the removed test asserts a repeated 165/5 sell pays nothing and leaves the snapshot byte-identical. The sibling does not check the 165/6 56-byte completion layout or remaining==1 after the sale. vendor_sell::sale_completion_id_drives_buy_back covers only the completion-id link with a different item and no sell-replay assertion. The sell-replay guarantee is plausibly covered by vendor_sell::replay_and_reload_cannot_pay_twice, but the cited replacement does not back it, and the ingredient-price and 165/6 layout assertions have no named replacement.
problems.fix: keep it (or split: keep the Bordon sell-back and replay assertions here, and only remove the buy-back-once portion that the sibling duplicates). Do not remove until the ingredient resale price, 165/6 layout and sell-replay refusal have a named covering test.

last_critiques.notes: The other six verdicts are keep, and I accept them: the refusal, persistence, canary and isolation tests have no removal recommended. whole_file_removable=false is correct. The auditor's claim that the sibling 'asserts at least as much' is not supported for the sell half. The auditor's own confidence (0.6) is consistent with a weak superseded call. The id check was clean and no cross notes were given.

The audit removes nothing: all seven tests are marked keep with covered_by null, and whole_file_removable is false. Keep verdicts cannot lose coverage, so the removal-side lens checks do not apply to any entry. The earlier 'superseded' verdict on selling_an_ingredient_back_uses_the_store_price_and_is_once was correctly overturned, because the cited coin_store_siblings test sells a different item from a generic fixture and does not check the ingredient resale price or the 165/6 layout. I did not re-open the vendor_sell.rs refusal tests to confirm the audit's claim that they compare snapshots only. That claim matters only if the insufficient/full-bag section is later trimmed, and the audit itself says it should not be trimmed until those tests are strengthened. Any future removal of that section needs a byte-level replacement for the save-bytes refusal checks first.

problems.issue: Marked duplicate of derby_route.rs::a_reconnect_keeps_the_ledger_and_the_next_match_pays_again, but the covering test does not make the same assertions. I read both bodies. The shipped test (derby_shipped_package.rs:673-713) round-trips the whole Snapshot (snapshot -> serde -> Snapshot -> Gameplay::load) and asserts that the prior job survives: saved.profiles.active == before_job and game.active_profile() == Some(before_job). derby_route's test serialises only GameplayState and never checks the prior job or active profile. The shipped test also asserts the next instance id is above the ledger after a fresh match starts, and that starting a match leaves paid_matches unchanged. The covering test does not assert the prior-job restore at all, so removing this test would drop the only check of that behaviour in this path. The auditor admitted it did not read the bodies line by line. The verdict is unbacked.
problems.fix: keep it (revise verdict to keep, covered_by null). If trimming is wanted later, first add an explicit active-profile assertion to derby_route::a_reconnect_keeps_the_ledger_and_the_next_match_pays_again and cover the Snapshot-encoding round trip, then re-audit.

problems.issue: Keep verdicts are acceptable. Each has a named reason, and the shipped-content and refusal/canary assertions have no equally strong replacement. The 'could be trimmed' note on tests[1] is speculative and should not be acted on.

Its duplicate verdict fails the lens because the named covering test omits the prior-job restore and the Snapshot round trip. whole_file_removable=false is correct. Keeping the file is the right outcome. The audit should be corrected before any builder acts on it.

No test is marked for removal, so every removal-lens check is vacuous and whole_file_removable=false is correct. I checked the one claim that matters most, the reconnect test. derby_route.rs:1405-1450 (a_reconnect_keeps_the_ledger_and_the_next_match_pays_again) serialises and reloads only GameplayState and checks paid_matches, coins and derby_active. It does not check the prior job or the active profile, so the shipped-package test's Snapshot round trip and active-profile assertion are not duplicated there. Keeping it was the right call. The audit's weak spot is that it only read the reconnect and results tests in full. The refusal and content verdicts rest on the prior audit and an excerpt. That does not change any verdict, since all five are kept. The auditor's suggested follow-up (add an explicit active-profile assertion to derby_route's reconnect test) is optional and not a removal.

tests.name: private_dev_teleport_location_setter_is_progress_free_but_visit_rules_are_not
tests.reason: Pins that the location-only setter does not change opening progress while the ordinary visit does, and rejects NaN. Progress/refusal invariant; kept.

tests.name: private_chat_reaches_the_social_router_without_trace

answer.notes: All ten tests are kept; none is a verified duplicate, superseded or obsolete. Every test pins a distinct behaviour: packet layout, refusals, atomicity, persistence, regressions. Most are #[ignore] and need the private campaign, so I checked them by reading rather than running them. The most_similar list cites tests/multiplayer.rs::audit_content_social_delivers_without_trace as overlapping private_chat_reaches_the_social_router_without_trace, but that name does not exist in the repo, so the overlap could not be verified. Re-check that if the multiplayer file is found. The realm goto usages in gateway_npc_offer_runtime.rs and bot_acceptance_1016.rs may overlap the name lookup in content_npcs_support...; I kept it because it also covers the listing filter and visibility refresh.

last_critiques.notes: All ten tests are verdict keep, so there are no removal verdicts to back with a covering test. The lens requires evidence only for superseded, duplicate or obsolete removals, and none is claimed. whole_file_removable is false, which is consistent with the keep verdicts. The removal list is empty, so it can be handed over as it stands. Keeping redundant tests is the safe direction. Weak points that do not change any verdict: (1) the keep reasons for content_npcs_support_filtered_listing... and private_chat_reaches_the_social_router_without_trace rest on 'no equivalent found' searches rather than a verified non-overlap, so they should stay as keeps. (2) The most_similar entry audit_content_social_delivers_without_trace in tests/multiplayer.rs was not confirmed in the repo, and the audit flags this itself. If that test does exist, it could be a second cover for the chat canary, but the canary stays kept either way. (3) Most tests are #[ignore] and were checked by reading, not by running, so the auditor's confidence of 0.7 is reasonable.

tests.name: stone_heart_hideaway_is_singular_level_gated_and_pays_through_gateway_once
tests.reason: One end-to-end gateway test covering the Stone Heart entrance singularity (battle 12303 replaces the passive Legacy entrance), the level-13 gate refused across Go, portal Play and the developer start route with no state change, the simulator skipping ineligible levels, the arena spawn and objective, a real fight that pays the reward exactly once, a replayed melee paying nothing, reconnect persistence, and a duplicate results Close that changes nothing. Refusal, persistence and pay-once checks are all here. The only other references to battle 12303 (bandit_hideout_dungeon.rs:1504, sheep_watch_dungeon.rs:1048, thugamug_battle.rs:604, brawler_mongo_chain.rs:1197) are loader or table-row checks, not a gateway run through the entrance, level gate, fight and payout, so none supersedes this test.

answer.notes: The pack lists a single test, and the file body (583 lines) was read in full apart from lines 1-250, which were covered by the excerpt. The file is one long monolithic scenario, so any future split would be a refactor rather than a removal. Cross-file overlap exists only at the data level: dungeon loader rows for 12303 (bandit, sheep_watch, thugamug) and brawler_mongo_chain's table check. The fixed-position NPC GUID checks in power_up_use.rs use STONE_HEART as a target and do not exercise the hideaway gate or payout. Confidence is limited because the similar-file list came from the pack and I did not read those files' assertions in detail.

last_critiques.notes: The audit removes nothing. Its single verdict is keep, and whole_file_removable is false, so the lens's requirement that every removal be backed by a named covering test does not apply. The only cross-file references it cites (bandit_hideout_dungeon.rs:1504, sheep_watch_dungeon.rs:1048, thugamug_battle.rs:604, brawler_mongo_chain.rs:1197) are described as loader or table-row checks, and keeping the test is the conservative outcome in any case. Minor weaknesses that do not change the verdict: the notes say lines 1-250 were 'covered by the excerpt' when the excerpt cuts off mid-helper around line 250, and the similar-file assertions were not read in detail. Neither affects a keep decision. The test name and the coverage list (level-13 refusal with no state change, pay-once, replay, reconnect, duplicate Close) are the checks a removal would have had to replace, so retaining the file as-is is the right call.

tests.name: integration_instance_ids_are_never_reused_after_a_top_row_retires

tests.name: integration_restart_never_reuses_a_retired_top_instance_id

tests.name: integration_a_replayed_consume_cannot_retarget_a_reused_id
tests.reason: Hostile-input check that a replayed consume cannot retarget a reused id. No equivalent test was found in the similar files.

tests.name: candidate_counter_is_monotonic_across_retire_and_restart
tests.reason: Same counter, same reopen-after-deleting-top-row sequence, same monotonic assertion. The floor-above-live-ids part is covered by piece_081::counter_hands_out_ids_above_every_live_instance.

tests.name: candidate_counter_burns_an_id_when_the_grant_never_lands
tests.reason: The burn comes from persisting the id before it is returned, which piece_081 checks directly. Reopen behaviour is also covered by counter_persists_across_reopen. Not a fully identical assertion, so confidence is moderate.

tests.name: candidate_counter_repairs_the_floor_and_exhausts_without_writing
tests.reason: Only the combination is unique here: floor repair is persisted, and exhaustion leaves the document byte-unchanged. piece_081 covers each half separately (counter_recovers_from_a_lost_or_stale_document and counter_refuses_to_exceed_the_instance_id_bound). tests.name: candidate_counter_refuses_ambiguous_or_corrupt_ids
tests.reason: Refusal test for duplicate ids, zero ids, unknown schema and a stale counter. Not removable without an equal check, and none is named in the similar files.

tests.name: integration_quest_turn_in_is_atomic_when_the_bag_is_full
tests.reason: Drives the production turn-in with a full bag and checks coins, rewarded flag and items stay unchanged. No other file in the pack covers the 069 turn-in path. It is expected to fail until gameplay.rs stages the reward, which is a reason to keep it, not remove it.

tests.name: integration_a_failed_turn_in_is_not_persisted_as_a_partial_reward

tests.name: candidate_ledger_records_intent_before_apply_and_settles_after

tests.name: candidate_ledger_settles_from_persisted_state_and_refuses_unproven_rewards
tests.reason: Refusal and no-double-grant check: settles from persisted state, and rejects an already-rewarded quest that the ledger never recorded. Persistence and refusal, so keep.

tests.name: candidate_ledger_refuses_stale_attempts_without_a_second_intent

tests.name: guard_coin_balance_refuses_overflow_and_keeps_the_bundle_atomic

tests.name: guard_full_bag_observation_for_the_086_bounds

tests.name: guard_reward_producers_stay_once_only_in_the_golden_path

answer.notes: The file is a mix: several integration_ tests are expected to fail until production call sites are patched, and the candidate_ tests pin the 081/069 modules. The two clearest removals are the duplicates of piece_081 (the reuse test and the simulated-restart monotonic test). The piece_081 reuse test is slated for deletion once inventory.rs uses the counter, so the integration_ version is the durable check and should be kept then. I did not read piece_069.rs or the full list of similar-file tests, so the turn-in and ledger verdicts rest on the test names and the excerpt. The earlier answer was cut off after candidate_counter_refuses_ambiguous_or_corrupt_ids; this answer covers all 17 tests.

problems.issue: Marked duplicate of tests/piece_081.rs::production_reward_never_reuses_a_retired_top_instance_id. That covering test is a temporary pin: its own doc says 'delete it when inventory.rs takes its id from the counter'. Once it is deleted, nothing checks the production retire-then-grant path. The integration test is the only lasting check of that path and must survive. The path and assertion match, but the covering test is not durable. (Its different definition id, 102 instead of 1195, is minor.)

candidate_counter_is_monotonic_across_retire_and_restart is marked duplicate of counter_stays_monotonic_across_a_simulated_restart_after_deleting_the_top_row. The reopen-and-allocate part is covered. The third step (open over [2,3,5] gives 6) is covered only in shape by counter_hands_out_ids_above_every_live_instance (live [2,5,7] gives 8). The auditor accepts this. Removal is defensible, but the floor-above-live-ids step is only analogous, not identical.
problems.fix: remove (acceptable), or keep the floor step if the builder wants exact coverage

problems.issue: candidate_counter_burns_an_id_when_the_grant_never_lands is marked superseded by counter_records_an_id_before_handing_it_out plus counter_persists_across_reopen. I checked those: the first checks the persisted value is first+1 before return, and the second checks reopen gives the next id. Together they cover the burn behaviour. Acceptable.

candidate_counter_repairs_the_floor_and_exhausts_without_writing is marked superseded, but the reason admits that neither piece_081 test covers both halves. The floor half is covered by counter_recovers_from_a_lost_or_stale_document (stale [1] over live [99] gives 100 and is persisted). The exhaustion half is covered by counter_refuses_to_exceed_the_instance_id_bound (byte-equal document). Each half is covered, so removal is defensible, but the verdict is weaker than the evidence needed for a refusal test. The builder should check that both halves are present in the replacement set.
problems.fix: remove only if the builder confirms both piece_081 tests are in the final set

problems.issue: Reported false, which is correct. The notes also say the piece_081.rs tests are the same module via #[path]. Those tests are compiled in both binaries, so the covering tests are not an independent second check. Keeping integration_instance_ids_are_never_reused_after_a_top_row_retires fixes the removal list.

last_critiques.notes: I checked the piece_081.rs covering tests for the counter, floor-repair, exhaustion, burn and production-reuse cases, and the candidate_counter_* bodies in economy_review.rs. The keep verdicts for the integration_, candidate_ledger_, guard_ and refusal tests were not verified because piece_069.rs and the golden-path tests were not in the read set, so those verdicts stay provisional. The main defect is the removal of the production retire-then-grant test, whose only covering test is a temporary pin. The counter removals are mostly backed.

problems.issue: Marked duplicate of piece_081::production_reward_never_reuses_a_retired_top_instance_id, but that test is a temporary pin: its own doc comment says 'delete it when inventory.rs takes its id from the counter'. Once the allocator is patched, the piece_081 test is deleted and the economy integration test is the only permanent guard on production id reuse. Both currently fail on the same assertion, so neither is an equal replacement. The auditor also admits it did not confirm that the piece_081 test drives production Inventory (the test does call f.inventory().grant/consume, so it does, but that does not make it a durable replacement).

candidate_counter_is_monotonic_across_retire_and_restart has a third step (open with live ids [2,3,5] floors to 6) that is not in counter_stays_monotonic_across_a_simulated_restart_after_deleting_the_top_row. The floor-above-live part is only partly covered by counter_hands_out_ids_above_every_live_instance (live [2,5,7] -> 8), which is a different case. The verdict is acceptable only if the floor step is accepted as covered; the audit does not say that explicitly.
problems.fix: keep it (or keep the file's floor assertion and drop only the first two steps)

problems.issue: candidate_counter_burns_an_id_when_the_grant_never_lands marked superseded by counter_records_an_id_before_handing_it_out. The piece_081 test checks the persisted value is first+1 and that the next id differs, which covers the burn mechanism. The economy test's reopen-returns-2 step is the same as counter_persists_across_reopen. Acceptable as superseded.

candidate_counter_repairs_the_floor_and_exhausts_without_writing is marked superseded, but its exhaustion part is covered by counter_refuses_to_exceed_the_instance_id_bound and its floor part by counter_recovers_from_a_lost_or_stale_document. Both pieces are covered by named tests, so the verdict holds. The auditor's own note calls it weaker.
Correctly false. The integration_ tests are the only permanent production-path checks, and the keep verdicts for refusal, persistence and atomicity tests are sound.

last_critiques.notes: Removing the list as given is not safe. The one removal that matters is tests[0]: it drops the only durable production-path guard against instance id reuse, because the named replacement is a temporary pin scheduled for deletion. Restore it as keep. The superseded counter verdicts (tests[4], tests[5]) and the monotonic duplicate (tests[3]) check out against piece_081.rs lines 185-404. I did not read the two turn-in integration tests or the ledger tests in full; their keep verdicts are conservative and not contradicted by the evidence I read. The auditor's confidence of 0.45 is appropriate.

last_critiques.notes: All 12 tests in tests/emotes.rs are marked keep with covered_by null, and whole_file_removable is false. First, the audit's overlap claims with tests/piece_093.rs and tests/social_chat.rs are only partly checked; the auditor says it did not read social_chat.rs. Second, the note that a later cleanup could trim piece_093 cases is a future suggestion, not a removal, and should not be executed without the replacement checks the lens requires. The removal list is empty, so it can be handed to a builder as a keep-all instruction.

The only plausible overlap is the last test's giver check versus enabled_quest_reachability.rs, which was not opened. No obsolescence found: nothing in the file pins behaviour replaced by a later task, although the file was last changed by T465 for exclusive-quest layers. Confidence is moderate because I read the similar files only by name and test list, not by body.

last_critiques.notes: All seven tests are verdict 'keep' with covered_by null, and whole_file_removable is false. No removal, duplicate or obsolete verdict exists, so the evidence lens has no covering test to open and no removal to back. Keeping every test is the safe outcome, and the list can be handed to a builder as-is (nothing to remove). Two weaknesses stay open but do not change the verdicts. (1) The last test's 'kept conservatively' reason admits that tests/enabled_quest_reachability.rs::every_enabled_quest_has_a_drawable_giver was not read, so the overlap claim is unverified. answer.notes: I read only the helper section (lines 150-449) and the menu-offers similar file's header, not every test body, so verdicts rest mainly on test names and doc lines. All seven tests are marked keep, so no superseded, duplicate or obsolete verdict needs a covering test, and the lens's replacement requirement does not apply. whole_file_removable=false is consistent with the keep verdicts. answer.notes: Low-confidence audit: I read only lines ~1-560 of the 869-line file and skimmed the similar pack. No test is clearly a duplicate or superseded, and the file is security/refusal-heavy, so every test is kept. Not verified: lines 560-869 (AI, melee, pursuer, opening content, oracle tests); their verdicts are defaults. A follow-up should compare the 'results_count' and 'loss_presents' tests against tests/encounter_score.rs in full.

last_critiques.notes: The audit proposes no removals: all 17 tests are marked keep, and whole_file_removable is false. Under the lens, every removal verdict must be backed, and there are none, so nothing is unbacked. Keeping is the safe direction for a file this security- and refusal-heavy, so the list can be handed to a builder as it stands (an empty removal list). Quality gaps, none of which block the pass: (1) Lines 560-869 were never read. Verdicts for ai_is_bounded_loss_retry_and_far_attacks_do_not_award, melee_requires_contact_and_enemy_motion_attacks_have_native_animation, pursuer_reaches_real_scale_contact_without_rounding_stall_and_stops_after_aggro, world_stage_gates_targets_and_persists_individual_defeats, and actual_opening_content_and_community_packet_oracle rest on names and doc text alone. (2) The auditor noted a possible overlap between results_count_real_defeats_on_loss_restore_and_retry and loss_presents_results_without_zoning_and_retry_resets_presentation, and tests/encounter_score.rs::loss_total_row_stays_zero_and_keeps_the_real_defeat_count, but did not check them. Those overlaps are the place a future pruning pass would most plausibly remove something, so they need a line-by-line comparison before any removal. (3) The 'covered_by' field is null for every test, so the audit gives no replacement evidence to cite if a later pass removes one.

tests.reason: Covers a repeat tick not re-sending 39/47, a removal ACK (39/7) that must not exit, a wrong-instance close refused, and the bound-instance close exiting. tests/encounter.rs::terminal_results_wait_for_native_close_and_remove_ack_never_returns_to_world (line 249) overlaps the ACK and no-exit part, and native_close_requires_exact_current_instance covers the refusal. answer.notes: Verdicts are based on the three tests in the pack and the file's full text (lines 225-270 read directly). Shared-helper overlap was checked by name and by a few assertion lines in tests/encounter.rs, not by a full read of that file. The main overlap is with tests/encounter.rs (13 similar tests). The inline win golden is the strongest unique check. encounter.rs's fixture-driven version is gated on an environment variable, so it cannot replace this file. Possible future consolidation: move the repeat-tick and wrong-instance assertions into encounter.rs, then remove the duplicated checks here. No test was classed as obsolete.

last_critiques.notes: All three verdicts are keep and whole_file_removable is false, so no removal is proposed and no equally strong replacement is needed. Keeping is the safe direction under the lens, so the audit passes. I checked the one external claim that bears on the keep reasoning: tests/encounter.rs:804-805 marks native_results_close_and_terminal_packets_match_compiled_community_writers as #[ignore] and needs OSFR_NATIVE_RESULTS_VECTORS. It does not run by default at all, which is stronger than the audit's 'panics when unset', so the audit's conclusion that encounter_score.rs's inline WIN_GOLDEN is the only always-on check of the win total holds. Not verified: that results_count_real_defeats_on_loss_restore_and_retry (encounter.rs:90) asserts a zero total row on loss, which the audit itself flagged as unconfirmed. The keep verdict for the loss test does not depend on it, but the audit's 'covered_by: null' should stay as is until that is checked. The duplicate-presentation test's repeat-tick and wrong-instance assertions were also not confirmed in encounter.rs; keeping it is correct regardless. The overall score is held down by the unverified overlap checks and the audit's own low confidence (0.6).

last_critiques.notes: All six tests are marked keep and whole_file_removable is false, so no removal verdict needs a covering test. Under the lens, keeping a redundant test is the acceptable error, so the audit meets the standard. The keep reasons are sound: the refusal test (wrong_job_wrong_target_and_replay_change_nothing) and the reconnect persistence test (a_mid_quest_reconnect_keeps_progress_and_pays_no_extra) are protected by the refusal and persistence rules, and the Cleetus offer test is the only one named for both offers and their reward bundles. Two weaknesses are minor. First, the record-load test is kept on the grounds that its per-field pins are not shown to be identical to quest_job_xp.rs. That is a conservative choice, not a removal, so it does not block the pass. Second, the auditor says it did not read the tail of the final test or the copper test in full, and confidence is 0.6. This does not change any verdict, but a future trim should wait for a full read. The cross notes are empty and the automatic id check is clean. I did not re-verify the 'no other file offers these records' claim; it does not affect the outcome because the test is kept.

tests.name: a_reward_grant_failure_is_refused_without_changing_the_save
tests.reason: Refusal: failed payout must change no coins, items, XP or positions and must not finish the encounter. Persistence/refusal class.

tests.name: an_ungrantable_prize_quantity_is_refused_through_gameplay
tests.reason: Refusal for an over-stack prize quantity, with the content-validation precondition asserted. Refusal class.

tests.name: cancel_mid_battle_returns_to_the_marker_without_paying
tests.reason: Only check of the 41/109 mid-battle cancel path for field battles; asserts no payout and a replayed cancel changes nothing.

tests.name: closing_the_start_screen_releases_the_pending_go
tests.reason: Security-style check that a dismissed start screen cannot be replayed into a battle, via both Close and leave. Kept.

tests.name: another_begin_consumes_the_open_start_screen
tests.reason: Checks that a second start consumes the pending screen so its later Go is inert. Kept as a replay/refusal check.

tests.name: go_from_outside_the_marker_radius_is_inert
tests.reason: Distance revalidation on Go; refusal class. battle_prize_bag_preflight.rs has a go_from_id helper but no equivalent distance test was identified.

tests.name: go_while_knocked_out_refuses_instead_of_ending_the_session
tests.reason: Refusal that reopens the screen rather than disconnecting. Sibling dungeon files (bandit_hideout_dungeon, bixie_hive_dungeon, sheep_watch_dungeon) carry a similar 'knocked out' refusal, but they drive different battles and this one uses the shared field-damage path directly, so it is not a clear duplicate.

answer.notes: No test is clearly duplicated or superseded; the file is mostly refusal, persistence and route checks for the original five-battle roster. Overlaps worth a later look: every_prize_resolves (prize half vs bandit_hideout_dungeon::every_previewed_prize_resolves_for_the_shipped_catalogue), five_distinct (appended row vs bandit_hideout_dungeon::the_shipped_rows_are_unchanged_and_the_new_row_is_appended), and the knocked-out Go refusal across the dungeon files. Only partial reads of the similar files were done, and field_reload_atomicity.rs was not compared against the collision tests, so confidence is moderate.

last_critiques.notes: All 16 verdicts are keep, and whole_file_removable is false. The evidence lens asks for backing on removal verdicts, and there are none, so there is nothing to check against a covering test. The auditor's keep-by-default approach is the safe direction. Two keep reasons are hedged ("not verified to be fully duplicated in field_reload_atomicity.rs" and "a possible overlap ... was not fully compared"). That is a gap in the justification, not in the outcome, because keeping is safe. The overlap notes (every_prize_resolves vs bandit_hideout_dungeon, five_distinct vs the appended-row test) are also left for later and remove nothing. The automatic id check is empty and cross notes are empty. The removal list is empty, so it can be handed to a builder as is. A later pass could tighten the hedged keep reasons, but this is optional.

tests.name: no_field_camp_shares_ground_with_a_band_more_than_two_levels_away
tests.reason: Only test that checks pairwise spacing of every shipped field actor across bands more than two levels apart, using leash + aggro + chase margin. The similar files (field_camps_high_band, field_camps_elite_band, field_enemy_level_camps) check their own band populations and rewards, not cross-band separation. Not clearly covered elsewhere; kept conservatively.

tests.name: low_difficulty_battle_markers_are_clear_of_higher_bands
tests.reason: Unique check that difficulty 1-2 battle markers and the giver-to-world-enemy walks (F621) stay clear of higher-band camps. It is the only test that reads the opening giver positions and encounters.json walks. The fixture-vs-production drift it cannot see is a note, not a reason to remove it.

tests.name: a_level_three_player_at_each_starter_camp_is_hit_only_by_its_own_band
tests.reason: Behavioural canary that drives the real shared-field tick from each of the 12 W102 starter centres and asserts only starter-band attackers hit, at the authored scaled damage. It is the only test here that exercises live hit packets. Similar files check populations and rewards, not hit attribution.

answer.notes: All three tests are distinct, and no similar file was shown to assert the same cross-band separation, low-level walk, or starter hit attribution. I read only the tail of the file and did not open field_camps_elite_band.rs or field_enemy_level_camps.rs to compare assertions line by line, so a partial overlap with those files is possible. The low-level walk test takes its opening givers from tests/fixtures/quests/opening.json, not shipped content, so it can drift from production; that is a fidelity risk, not a redundancy. Lower confidence reflects that comparison gap.

last_critiques.notes: All three tests are marked keep, and whole_file_removable is false, so no removal verdict needs a covering test. Keeping is the conservative direction under this lens, so the audit's output is acceptable as written. The audit is weaker than it could be in two places. It admits it read only the tail of the file and did not open field_camps_elite_band.rs or field_enemy_level_camps.rs to compare assertions, so its claim that no similar file covers cross-band separation is unverified. Its keep reasons also lean on 'not clearly covered elsewhere' rather than a checked negative. Neither gap changes the outcome, because no test is removed. The low-level walk test's reliance on tests/fixtures/quests/opening.json is a fidelity risk the audit correctly flags as a note, not a removal reason.

tests.name: six_elite_camps_load_with_levels_fifteen_to_twenty
tests.reason: Only test that loads the six elite actors and three appended groups from the shipped field file and checks their levels, provenance, GUID order and group membership. The loader gate is unique to this content.

tests.name: every_elite_home_is_a_verified_w102_centre
tests.reason: Checks the T415 audited centre for each elite home and that the six centres are distinct. Overlaps the high-band centre test in spirit, but the data and centres differ, and it is not clearly covered elsewhere.

tests.name: the_elite_camps_spawn_in_on_zone_ready
tests.reason: Only check that the six elite actors spawn through the 35/2 path and that scaled HP rises with level. Not covered by another file for these actors.

tests.name: a_level_twenty_kill_pays_the_14_20_band_once
tests.reason: The 14-20 band payout overlaps tests/field_camps_high_band.rs::a_level_twenty_actor_pays_the_new_band, but this test also covers the one-payout replay check and a near-cap wallet/XP refusal with no half payout. That refusal is a keep case, so the test stays.

tests.name: a_level_fifteen_kill_pays_the_same_band_and_a_level_fourteen_control_still_pays_old
tests.reason: Pins that the actor level, not the player level, picks the band, with level-14 and level-10 controls. The high-band file has similar controls (level_thirteen_and_ten_controls_keep_the_nine_thirteen_band), but this test uses different actors and asserts the elite band row. Kept conservatively.

tests.name: two_players_share_an_elite_kill_and_each_is_paid_once
tests.reason: Shared-kill payout overlaps tests/field_kill_rewards.rs::a_shared_kill_pays_each_credited_player_once, but this test also covers the job switch between hit and claim (XP follows the active job) and the 180 s respawn timing. Those are not covered elsewhere.

tests.name: a_malformed_or_duplicate_elite_camp_is_refused_atomically
tests.reason: Refusal test: malformed field and reward tables are rejected and the live field and behaviour are unchanged. Refusal checks are kept.

tests.name: the_existing_camps_and_wolf_quest_are_unchanged
tests.reason: Canary: a SHA-256 digest of the pre-T332 prefix, the order of old actors and groups, the live wolf list, the 3000009 quest objective and the shipped 14-20 band values. Canaries are kept.

tests.name: the_uncovered_reward_level_or_definition_override_does_not_pay

The no-pay half overlaps tests/field_camps_high_band.rs::a_level_outside_the_bands_pays_nothing_without_an_error, but a refusal check is kept unless an equal test is named for both halves.

answer.notes: Every test here is kept. The file's tests mostly pin elite-specific data (GUIDs, centres, group members, the digest canary) that no other file checks. Several reward-band paths overlap tests/field_camps_high_band.rs and tests/field_kill_rewards.rs. I did not read those files' bodies, so the overlap is judged from their names only. If a later pass wants to trim, the best candidates are the first half of the level-20 band test and the shared-kill payout assertions, with the high-band and field_kill_rewards tests as the cover. I read the file's bodies from line 300 onward and the top of the file from the excerpt.

problems.issue: The overlap rationale for the level-20 band test, the level-15 test, and the shared-kill test cites tests/field_camps_high_band.rs and tests/field_kill_rewards.rs. The auditor says it judged those overlaps from file names only. The keep verdicts are still safe, but the stated reasons for keeping are not verified.

Every verdict is keep and whole_file_removable is false, so no removal is proposed and there is no removal to back. The lens's superseded or duplicate evidence checks are not triggered. The refusal, canary and persistence tests are kept, which matches the lens.

last_critiques.notes: No test is marked superseded, duplicate or obsolete, so there are no removal claims to check against covering tests. Keeping everything is the conservative outcome the lens prefers. The audit's notes say it read the file body only from line 300 onward and judged the rest from the excerpt, and it did not open the two overlapping suites. If a later pass wants to trim the level-20 or shared-kill tests, it should first open tests/field_camps_high_band.rs and tests/field_kill_rewards.rs and confirm the same path and assertion strength. The automatic id check was empty, so no ids are missing or invented.

tests.name: the_loader_accepts_the_high_camps_and_exposes_them
tests.reason: Loader canary: HIGH actors spawn via 35/2, expose authored level, leash, and HP scaled per level. Not covered by the elite file's spawn test, which checks different actors.

tests.name: the_high_camps_use_verified_w102_centres_and_unique_guids
tests.reason: Pins counts, unique GUIDs and spawn-area ids, centres, provenance kinds and group membership for the HIGH rows. The elite file only checks centres, so this is not a duplicate.

tests.name: a_level_fourteen_kill_pays_the_new_band_once
tests.reason: Band boundary (level 14 pays 18 coins and 35 XP) plus replay and corpse-hit no-double-pay checks. Not covered elsewhere in the set I read.

tests.name: the_active_job_not_the_actor_kind_receives_the_xp

tests.name: the_level_thirteen_and_ten_controls_keep_the_nine_thirteen_band
tests.reason: Boundary controls proving actor level, not player level, selects the band. Keep as the negative control for the band change.

tests.reason: Top-of-band payout (18 coins, 35 XP). It may overlap field_camps_elite_band.rs::a_level_twenty_kill_pays_the_14_20_band_once, but I did not read that test body, so I am not claiming it is superseded.

tests.name: a_level_outside_the_bands_pays_nothing_without_an_error
tests.reason: Refusal-style check: an uncovered level pays nothing and emits no error while the kill still happens.

tests.name: an_unclaimed_high_camp_credit_expires_or_is_lost_on_leaving_and_pays_nothing
tests.reason: Expiry and no-pay refusal check. Overlaps the generic credit-expiry tests in field_kill_rewards.rs, which I did not read, so keep to be conservative.

tests.name: two_players_share_a_high_camp_kill_and_each_is_paid_once
tests.reason: Shared-kill once-per-player check. Resembles field_kill_rewards.rs::a_shared_kill_pays_each_credited_player_once, but I did not compare assertions, so it is not marked duplicate.

tests.name: the_band_table_is_sorted_non_overlapping_and_bounded
tests.reason: Table-validity canary for overlapping and unbounded bands. Keep.

tests.name: a_malformed_high_camp_or_band_is_refused_atomically
tests.reason: Hostile-input refusal check with atomicity. Never removable without an equivalent named test.

answer.notes: Low confidence: I read only about 3/4 of the file's bodies (lines 1-520 and 520-819, not the last ~150 lines). I did not read field_kill_rewards.rs or the tail of field_camps_elite_band.rs (only its first 300 lines). The overlap with field_camps_elite_band.rs (same loader/digest/shared-kill/malformed structure, different actors) and with field_kill_rewards.rs is real, but the high-band tests pin different actors and band boundaries. Every verdict is keep. A follow-up should diff a_level_twenty_actor_pays_the_new_band and two_players_share_a_high_camp_kill_and_each_is_paid_once against their elite and field_kill_rewards counterparts before any removal.

last_critiques.notes: All 12 verdicts are keep, with covered_by null, so no removal is proposed and nothing is lost by handing this list to a builder. whole_file_removable is false, which is consistent with that. The only removal-relevant risk is the audit's own low confidence (0.3): it read about three quarters of the file, did not read field_kill_rewards.rs or the tail of field_camps_elite_band.rs, and flagged a_level_twenty_actor_pays_the_new_band, two_players_share_a_high_camp_kill_and_each_is_paid_once and the credit-expiry test as possible overlaps. Keeping them is the safe default. Several reasons also assert unverified facts, such as the elite file only checking centres and the elite existing-camps test being a weaker GUID/prefix check. Those claims do not change any keep verdict, but they should be checked before any later pruning. Follow-up: diff those three overlaps against field_camps_elite_band.rs and field_kill_rewards.rs before removing anything from this file.

tests.name: field_enemy_leashes_on_the_wire
tests.reason: The only test that checks the home leash through the packet stream of a live gateway (0x007d position updates, a 12.01 m bound, and return home). The engine-level leash checks in tests/field_enemies_runtime.rs::home_leash_returns_and_heals_while_ignoring_reaggro and tests/field_ai_packets.rs::leash_refuses_the_step_before_it_crosses run in-process and never exercise the wire path, so they do not cover it. It is a canary-style check of the shipped gateway, so keep it.

answer.notes: The file holds a single #[ignore]d test that needs W105_GATEWAY and W105_REFERENCE from scratch_gate.py, so it does not run in the default suite. It is not a duplicate of the in-process leash tests, though they overlap in intent. Its overlap is the leash-return idea in field_enemies_runtime.rs, which is the closest match. Its created_by and last_changed_by are null in the pack, so no task-based obsolescence applies. I did not check the bot module or the scratch_gate.py helper beyond the excerpt.

last_critiques.notes: The audit's only verdict is keep for field_enemy_leashes_on_the_wire, so no removal is proposed and whole_file_removable=false is consistent. I confirmed the three leash tests it cites exist: field_enemies_runtime.rs::home_leash_returns_and_heals_while_ignoring_reaggro, field_ai_packets.rs::leash_refuses_the_step_before_it_crosses, and field_enemies_bot.rs::field_enemy_leashes_on_the_wire. I did not open the bodies of the two in-process tests to confirm that they never touch the wire path. That claim supports the keep, and a keep needs no replacement, so it does not change the outcome. The audit's own caveats (ignored test needing scratch_gate.py, bot module not inspected) are honest. The file was not checked against the quest answers, and the id check was empty.

tests.name: home_leash_returns_and_heals_while_ignoring_reaggro
tests.reason: Leash-home-and-heal with re-aggro ignored, with an explicit canary comment. field_ai_packets.rs has leash/evade pins, but those assert the ordered wire frames, not this state-level home-and-heal path with a nearby player.

tests.name: kill_then_respawn_forgets_skill_effects
tests.reason: Refusal-style check that a field-enemy respawn clears stun, debuff and DoT. encounter_job_skills covers knockout and session reset of the player, not enemy respawn, so it is not an equivalent test.

tests.name: evade_completion_forgets_skill_effects
tests.reason: Same effect-clearing guarantee, on evade completion rather than kill. Distinct trigger path.

tests.name: reload_field_enemies_forgets_skill_effects
tests.reason: Same effect-clearing guarantee, on reload_field_enemies. Distinct path; state-clearing is a persistence/reset guarantee.

tests.name: roaming_is_seeded_bounded_and_pauses
tests.reason: Seeded determinism and leash bound for field-enemy roaming. field_ai_packets::wanderer_arrives_pauses_and_resumes exercises battle-marker wanderers, a different actor source; not verified as equivalent.

tests.name: levels_scale_hp_damage_and_respawn
tests.reason: Checks level-scaled HP, hit and respawn. combat_scale.rs has a_field_enemy_keeps_its_hits_to_kill_and_hits_to_die and enemy_rows_are_scaled_once_where_they_load, which overlap in part, but this test drives the runtime tick/attack/respawn path. Conservative keep.

tests.name: a_field_enemy_hit_follows_its_row_damage_and_level
tests.reason: T398 regression pin that the hit is derived from the row's damage and level through the data scale. Overlaps combat_scale::enemy_rows_are_scaled_once_where_they_load in intent, but asserts the runtime hit after editing the row; keep.

tests.name: behaviour_leash_fallback_and_honest_stationary_reach
tests.reason: Covers the behaviour.leash fallback when leash_radius is null, and stationary reach boundary (2.6 m refused, 2.5 m hits). Not found elsewhere in this exact form.

tests.name: roaming_follows_existing_terrain_heights
tests.reason: Verifies roaming Y follows the bound terrain grid. Only check of terrain-following for field enemies in the similar files; keep.

tests.name: malformed_metadata_and_positions_fail_without_replacing_field
tests.reason: Hostile-input and refusal check: malformed metadata, NaN/inf positions, and rejected reload preserving the field and attack cooldown. Security/refusal test; no equally strong copy found.

answer.notes: Audited from the file's full text and the first 300 lines of field_ai_packets.rs (the most similar file, which pins ordered wire frames for leash, evade and wanderer behaviour). I did not read the rest of field_ai_packets.rs, field_battle_roster.rs, or combat_scale.rs in detail, so the overlap calls are based on test names. Nothing is marked removable: every test is a state-level check, the file is a distinct runtime fixture, and the guidance is to keep when unsure. Possible follow-up: compare levels_scale_hp_damage_and_respawn and roaming_is_seeded_bounded_and_pauses against combat_scale.rs and field_ai_packets.rs::wanderer_arrives_pauses_and_resumes for real duplication.

last_critiques.notes: No test is marked superseded, duplicate or obsolete, and whole_file_removable is false, so there are no removal verdicts that need a named replacement. Every verdict is keep, which is the conservative outcome under the lens. Two weaknesses remain in the keep reasons, but they do not change any removal decision. First, several reasons say the overlap with combat_scale.rs and field_ai_packets.rs was judged from test names only (levels_scale_hp_damage_and_respawn, roaming_is_seeded_bounded_and_pauses, a_field_enemy_hit_follows_its_row_damage_and_level). The auditor says so itself, so a later pass could check them for real duplication. Second, the claim that no equivalent exists for the leash, run-speed and effect-clearing tests is asserted, not checked against the covering files. Both gaps only matter if someone later wants to remove a test from this file. Recommendation: keep all 11 tests, and if a future audit wants to trim, read combat_scale.rs::a_field_enemy_keeps_its_hits_to_kill_and_hits_to_die and field_ai_packets.rs::wanderer_arrives_pauses_and_resumes first.

tests.name: starter_enemies_and_camps_stay_inside_the_final_era_budget
tests.reason: The only test in the suite that checks the (R) time-to-knock-out budget for starter field enemies and starter camps, measured from the live engine (player health after set_player_job, hits from attack_processed). The similar files pin content identity, loader bounds, banding, separation and shared-state behaviour, not the combat-time floor. Nothing else drives this path with these assertions, so it is not superseded or duplicate. Bounds check, not a redundant copy.

answer.notes: Single test, created and last changed by T398. Its doc describes the budget as tunable bounds, so a later retuning of combat_scale.json or the budget constants would legitimately break it; that is a maintenance cost, not redundancy. The nearest file, tests/field_enemy_level_camps.rs (T245/T699), pins level bands, GUIDs, loader bounds and balance rows for the same content but does not assert time-to-knock-out. Searching the repo for the budget constants and the 'knocks out' assertion found no other test with these floors. Not checked: whether tests/field_camp_separation.rs or the power_up_drops suite compute player-kill timing in a way that overlaps; the excerpts I saw do not.

last_critiques.notes: The audit proposes no removals: its single test is marked keep, and whole_file_removable is false, so there is no superseded, duplicate or obsolete verdict to back with a covering test. I checked the keep rationale. The 90 s lone and 30 s camp floors, computed from the engine's player_health after set_player_job and from attack_processed hits over the shipped field_enemies.json, appear only in starter_enemies_and_camps_stay_inside_the_final_era_budget. A repo search for knock-out and floor-constant terms found no other test asserting these time-to-knock-out floors. The closest, tests/combat_scale.rs (health curve, hits-to-kill on a synthetic 180/25 enemy, heal ladder), uses fixture data and does not check shipped starter content against the time budget, so it does not supersede this test. Caveat: the auditor's confidence of 0.8 is reasonable. The audit did not inspect field_camp_separation.rs or power_up_drops.rs for player-kill timing, and I did not close that gap, but it does not change the keep verdict.

tests.name: four_mid_level_camps_load_with_valid_bands_and_ids
tests.reason: Only test that drives the real loader over the four mid-level camps (bands, levels, group membership, field_roamer leash/aggro, 35/2 visibility, engine.field_level). Field_camps_high_band and field_camps_elite_band cover other camps, not these rows.

tests.name: every_new_home_is_a_verified_w102_centre
tests.reason: Checks the eight mid-camp homes against verified_centre and for uniqueness. The sibling tests cover the high (tests/field_camps_high_band.rs::the_high_camps_use_verified_w102_centres_and_unique_guids) and elite (tests/field_camps_elite_band.rs::every_elite_home_is_a_verified_w102_centre) sets only, so this is a different scope. tests.name: the_actor_and_group_counts_stay_inside_the_loader_bounds
tests.reason: The 34-actor and 13-group totals duplicate field_camps_elite_band.rs lines ~402-403 ("28 pre-T332 + 6 elite", "10 pre-T332 + 3 elite"), but the 128 KiB file bound, the 64 actor/group caps and the every-row provenance/evidence (R)-prefix check are not found elsewhere. tests.reason: Pins starter stats, provenance shape, and quest-gated Hooligan identity/gate for the 12 starter and 4 quest rows. Overlaps the digest pins in tests/field_camps_high_band.rs (EXISTING_ACTORS) and tests/field_camps_elite_band.rs::the_existing_camps_and_wolf_quest_are_unchanged, which I did not read in full; those are stronger for identity but this test checks field-level values and the quest gate explicitly. answer.notes: All four tests are mostly unique to the mid-level camps or to field-level invariants. Overlap is real but partial: the count totals (34/13) are duplicated in field_camps_elite_band.rs, and the starter/quest pin overlaps the digest-based pins in field_camps_high_band.rs. The test bodies of the high/elite 'existing unchanged' tests were not read in full, so no superseded verdicts were issued. Nothing here is obsolete: the 34/13 totals match the current content, and T699 touched the sibling files, not this one's assertions.

last_critiques.notes: All four tests are kept, so no removal verdict needs a covering test. I checked the one factual overlap claim: field_camps_elite_band.rs lines 402-403 do assert 34 actors and 13 groups, so the count duplication the audit reports is real. The file's own 34/13 comments match its asserts, and the 30 always-on count in the first test is consistent with the 12+8+4+6 comment. The audit's keep reasons for the count test (128 KiB bound, 64 caps, the (R) provenance check) are not duplicated in the elite file's count test, so keeping it is justified. The audit did not read the bodies of field_camps_high_band.rs::the_existing_camps_and_rewards_are_unchanged or field_camps_elite_band.rs::the_existing_camps_and_wolf_quest_are_unchanged in full (it says so itself). Its 'conservative keep' on the starter/quest test is therefore unverified, but since it removes nothing, this does not change the outcome. Whole-file removal is correctly rejected. Before any future consolidation, someone should read those two 'unchanged' bodies to confirm the field-level pins are really redundant.

tests.name: starting_regions_have_grouped_reconstructed_placements_and_presets

tests.reason: Drives the shipped starter wolf end to end: spawn, roam within the 6 m disc, kill, the 45 s group timer not expiring at 44,999 ms, respawn at home with full health. field_enemies_runtime.rs covers respawn and leash only on a synthetic fixture with respawn_seconds 1, not the authored group timer on shipped content.

tests.name: malformed_group_reload_is_atomic
tests.reason: Same mutation: a spawn group with members [GUID, GUID] is refused by reload_field_enemies with world targets and the enemy's behaviour unchanged. The elite-band test runs the same duplicate-member refusal on shipped content and also checks level-band and off-centre refusals. answer.notes: Pack excerpt appears to be the whole file (247 lines, 3 tests). The third test's removal depends on field_camps_elite_band.rs asserting the same before/after state; I checked only the mutation list and the start of the assertions, not its full body.
