answer.notes: Verified bodies: fishing_review.rs session_binding_lifecycle, refused_requests_leave_the_session_untouched, and the native_cast_anim NaN check. Other superseded verdicts rest on names and the earlier review notes. The four keeps are the envelope refusals, the server layouts, the SpawnFishRun byte layout, and the ordering and foreign-Cast gaps. Removing the superseded tests would also drop the Special header check and the foreign-Cast case, so consider folding those two into the review file before deleting this file.

problems.issue: header_is_two_u16_fields is marked superseded, but the covering test native_envelope_and_register_field_order (fishing_review.rs:139-162) only checks the envelope on a RegisterPlayer frame (sub 2). Nothing in the review file asserts the Special (sub 15) header bytes [0x8a,0x00,0x0f,0x00] or the 12-byte Special length. The auditor's own reason says Special sub 15 is the unique part.
problems.fix: keep it (or rewrite it as a Special-only check and keep the sub-15 assertion)

problems.issue: every_recovered_request_round_trips is marked superseded by deterministic_byte_scan_never_panics_and_round_trips (fishing_review.rs:391-412). That scan only round-trips whatever random bytes happen to decode. It does not guarantee that each of the five variants, especially CastAnim with its NaN-free vec4 payload and Special, is round-tripped. The explicit five-variant round trip is not replaced.

session_enforces_recovered_ordering is said to be covered by refused_requests_leave_the_session_untouched, but the cited OutOfOrder and Duplicate assertions (review lines 519 and 540) sit in session_binding_lifecycle (508-571). The auditor inferred the covering name from a line range and did not read refused_requests (574+). Reel-in-before-cast ordering is not shown to be covered by any named test.
problems.fix: keep it until the reel-in ordering assertion is found in a named replacement and that test is read

problems.issue: session_rejects_requests_from_a_foreign_actor is cited to refused_requests_leave_the_session_untouched, but the ForeignActor assertions it cites (review 549/553) are in session_binding_lifecycle and cover only RegisterPlayer and Special. Foreign Cast and ReelIn refusals, which the original test asserts, are not verified in the covering test.
problems.fix: keep it, or confirm Cast and ReelIn foreign refusals in refused_requests_leave_the_session_untouched (574+) and cite that line range

problems.issue: session_rejects_a_result_for_a_foreign_actor is cited to foreign_and_unbound_results_are_refused (fishing_review.rs:807), which was never opened. The verdict rests on the name alone, and the lens requires the covering test to be checked.
problems.fix: keep it until foreign_and_unbound_results_are_refused is read and shown to assert ForeignActor with the session left Idle

problems.issue: request_lengths_match_native_writers is backed only by request_bodies_are_exact_length (fishing_review.rs:415). That test was not read past its opening, so the 13/32/29/13/12 values are not confirmed.
problems.fix: keep it until request_bodies_are_exact_length is read and the five exact lengths are confirmed

problems.issue: Correctly false. The file has unique refusal and byte-layout tests, and the auditor's own keep verdicts show this.

last_critiques.notes: Removal backed: re_registration_and_reset_policy (binding_lifecycle asserts Duplicate, ForeignActor, reset unbind), wire_codec_stays_lossless (NAN_BITS to_bits check at review 221-229). Partly backed, needs a read: session tests and request lengths. Cross notes and id check were empty. Confidence 0.5 is about right: several verdicts rest on inferred names. Keeps for the SpawnFishRun layout, envelope refusals and NaN/negative refusals are sound.

problems.issue: every_recovered_request_round_trips is marked superseded by fishing_review.rs::deterministic_byte_scan_never_panics_and_round_trips. The scan only round-trips requests that happen to decode from random bytes, so it almost never reaches a Cast, ReelIn or Special frame. fishing_review.rs never calls .encode() on a Cast, ReelIn or Special value (the only encode() calls are RegisterPlayer at lines 159-160, CastAnim at 215 and 233, and the scan at 401). Encode-side coverage for three of five variants is lost.
problems.fix: keep it, or first add encode-equals-bytes and decode(encode(case))==case assertions for Cast, ReelIn and Special to fishing_review.rs, then remove.

problems.issue: request_lengths_match_native_writers asserts encode().len() of 13/32/29/13/12. fishing_review.rs::request_bodies_are_exact_length only checks decode acceptance and refusal of frames built by frame()/handle_bytes, not encoder output. The encoder lengths for Cast (29), ReelIn (13) and Special (12) have no other check in the review file. The auditor admitted it read only the name.
problems.fix: keep it, or add encode().len() assertions for Cast, ReelIn and Special to fishing_review.rs before removing.

problems.issue: header_is_two_u16_fields is marked superseded. native_envelope_and_register_field_order covers the 0x8a 0x00 0x02 0x00 encoder envelope for RegisterPlayer, and the Special decode at line 267 covers sub 15. The Special encoder header bytes [2..4]==[15,0] and OPCODE==138 are not asserted anywhere in the review file. The loss is small, but the verdict is not fully backed.
problems.fix: keep it, or add an assert on Special.encode() header bytes to the review file before removing.

problems.issue: The verdicts on session_binding_lifecycle, refused_requests_leave_the_session_untouched, invalid_results_do_not_mutate_the_session and foreign_and_unbound_results_are_refused are supported by the bodies I read (session_binding_lifecycle, refused_requests up to line 600). The review file's NaN bit-pattern check at lines 219-233 backs the wire_codec removal. I did not read the rest of refused_requests (the -0.5 case) or foreign_and_unbound_results, so those are only partly verified.
problems.fix: keep it as is for the verified removals; confirm the -0.5 refusal and the foreign-result body before submitting those removals.

last_critiques.notes: The kept tests are correct. decode_rejects_bad_envelopes is the only check of WrongOpcode (0x8b) in either file. The review file's ordering checks, which the auditor kept, are present at fishing.rs lines 284-357 and the review file's session_binding_lifecycle and refused_requests, so keeping session_enforces_recovered_ordering and session_rejects_requests_from_a_foreign_actor is conservative and fine. Overall the file is not removable yet: the removal list for tests[1] and tests[2] lacks encode-side evidence for Cast, ReelIn and Special, so the removal list is not wireable as it stands.

The most similar files (kart_service, player_trade, kart_npc_entry, housing_service, vendor_sell) are different subsystems and do not duplicate fishing paths. problems.issue: Verdict 'duplicate' is mostly backed: casting_again_after_a_catch_pays_the_next_catch_once_more (lines 774-783) drives the same Round::catch loop and asserts fish_held and fisherman_xp per catch. problems.fix: Either keep it, or move the coins()==0 assertion into casting_again_after_a_catch_pays_the_next_catch_once_more before removing the duplicate. Its name also implies a cap-off mode the body never sets up, so rename or retitle if it is kept.

problems.issue: Verdict 'superseded' by tests/fishing_service.rs::early_reel_escapes_without_grant is only partly backed. The source signature (src/game_rules.rs:294) is (kind: i16, is_member: bool), which matches the repo test, not the pack. The audit's note that the excerpt is stale is correct, but the doc comment on this test still describes the old layout and should be updated to match the two-argument encoder. answer.notes: Single test, classified keep because it is the only switching/persistence check across all seven jobs. Overlap is partial: the level-ladder and Adventurer-clears-slots assertions are largely duplicated in tests/opening_abilities.rs (every_job_bar_has_exactly_the_unlocked_ladder_at_every_level, noncombat_class_clears_all_eight_slots_and_invalid_profile_fails, brawler_level_boundaries). If the team wants to trim, the Brawler and Adventurer blocks are the removable parts, but the test as a whole should stay. problems.issue: Verdict is keep with covered_by null, so no removal is claimed and there is no covering test to verify. The uncertainty only means a possible overlap, and overlap is safe to keep under the lens.

last_critiques.notes: No test is marked superseded, duplicate or obsolete, and whole_file_removable is false, so the lens's requirement to open covering tests for removal verdicts does not apply. The Brawler and Adventurer blocks are the only parts the auditor flagged as partly duplicated in tests/opening_abilities.rs, and that overlap is not a reason to remove the test now. Overlapping coverage: tests/job_trainers.rs:1093 (bare unlocked job switch emits repaired outfit, F155), tests/job_trainers.rs:1147 and :853 (learning does not duplicate starter grants), tests/bot_acceptance_1016.rs (same-job outfit repair broadcast). last_critiques.notes: The only test, private_switching_to_a_bare_job_dresses_it, is marked keep, so no removal is proposed and whole_file_removable=false is consistent. I confirmed the two cited synthetic tests exist in tests/job_trainers.rs (selecting_a_bare_unlocked_job_emits_an_activation_from_the_repaired_outfit at line 1093, learning_does_not_increase_owned_starter_quantities at line 1147). The keep rationale is sound: it is the only check that runs against the real private Kart Driver (profile 48) save, it is #[ignore]d so it adds no default-run cost, and it asserts a no-duplicate reswitch invariant on that save. The auditor's claim that the synthetic tests cover the mechanism is only partly verified: I checked that they exist, not that they assert the same no-duplicate count. That gap does not change the keep verdict, since keeping is the safe direction. Confidence 0.7 is reasonable.

tests.reason: Hostile-input and refusal check: bit flips in header bytes, a forged item-use opcode (19), out-of-range lengths, a corrupted CRC and every truncation. No other test drives this decoder, so nothing equivalent exists elsewhere.

tests.name: direct_pose_requires_single_complete_zlib_stream_and_supported_flag
tests.reason: Refusal check for unsupported flag values, trailing bytes or concatenated zlib streams, and an output cap that is too small. Security-relevant and unique to this decoder.

answer.notes: All three tests are the only checks of decode_kart_pose_datagram (src/soe.rs:176) in the repo's tests directory. The similar files (kart_service.rs, transport_fuzz.rs, kart_weapons.rs) test the kart service, the generic SOE transport parser and the weapon codecs; they do not call this decoder, so none supersedes these tests. transport_fuzz.rs covers zlib bombs and trailing bytes for the general transport, not this datagram format, so it is not a true equivalent. I did not read the decoder body, so the verdicts rest on the test code and the grep, not on a line-by-line comparison of assertions.

last_critiques.notes: All three tests are verdict 'keep' with covered_by null, and whole_file_removable is false, so there are no removal verdicts to back. The lens requirement (named replacement for superseded or duplicate tests) does not apply. I checked the key evidence claim: a repo search for decode_kart_pose_datagram finds calls only in this test file (lines 30 to 92) and in the production gateway (src/bin/osfr-gateway.rs:1256) and its definition (src/soe.rs:176). No other test file calls the decoder, so the 'unique coverage' reasons hold. The audit did not read the decoder body, so its assertion-level comparison is unverified; that gap does not change any verdict because nothing is removed. Minor: the 'keep' reasons are thin (for example, 'Security-relevant and unique' is asserted, not shown). That does not warrant a change.

last_critiques.notes: The audit proposes no removals: all ten tests are keep, covered_by is null throughout, and whole_file_removable is false. Under the evidence lens, the pass condition is that every removal verdict is backed, and no removal verdict exists, so nothing is removed on weak grounds. Keeping all ten is the conservative direction the lens prefers. The removal list is empty, so it can be handed to a builder as is. Weaknesses that do not change the outcome: (1) the audit admits it read only the first four test bodies in the excerpt and did not open the similar files (kart_service.rs, kart_npc_entry.rs) for line-level comparison, so its 'not a duplicate' and 'not clearly covered' claims for tests 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 and 10 are unverified; (2) the test-4 reason says 'Body not fully read', so its keep rests on the name alone; (3) the claim that kart_service.rs gate-band and curtain tests are 'geometry-only' was not checked. A later pass that wants to trim this file should first read the bodies of tests 4-10 and compare them with the named synthetic tests before proposing any removal. The file's #[ignore] status means it is low-cost to keep.

answer.notes: All three tests are #[ignore]d and require private env inputs (OSFR_KART_LOBBY_CONTENT, OSFR_GATEWAY_REFERENCE), so they likely do not run in the default suite; that is a cost/visibility issue, not redundancy. Similar files (kart_npc_entry, housing_session, housing_service, type8_harvesting_gateway, login_broker) test different activities and do not drive opcode 102/0/1/0. kart_lobby_native.rs covers the codec (including oversized counts and text) and bundle_activity_content.rs only reads/encodes kart_lobby.json; I did not inspect bundle_activity_content.rs in full, so a load-refusal overlap there is not fully ruled out. The keep reasons are conservative and the named overlaps checked out: activity_portal.rs:215 asserts parse(&[102,0,1,0]) is None, and bundle_activity_content.rs reads and encodes kart_lobby.json (lines 181-182). That gap only matters if someone later proposes removing the load-refusal test, and it does not affect this pass. The auditor's cost note is valid: all three tests are #[ignore]d and need private env inputs, so they never run in the default suite. answer.notes: All six tests are T379-specific content and refusal checks on two actor GUIDs (1000000001989 / 1000000002048, content keys 9000001989 / 9000002048). Possible consolidation, not removal: the far/wrong refusal and two-player tests could be folded into a shared NPC harness later, but that is a refactor, not a redundancy. I did not verify the full bodies of the similar files' tests beyond names and their listed docs.

last_critiques.notes: The audit proposes no removals. All six tests are marked keep, and whole_file_removable is false, so there are no superseded, duplicate or obsolete verdicts to back with a covering test. The lens therefore has nothing to reject. The keep rationales are conservative. The refusal, two-session and busy-player tests are kept even where similar tests exist in fishing_guide_drawable, priced_vendors_drawable, minigame_entry_npcs and kart_npc_entry, which is the safe direction under the lens. Two weaknesses to note, neither a blocker: (1) the auditor says it did not verify the bodies of the similar files' tests beyond names, so the claim that the T379 GUID-specific assertions have no peer is unproven; this only matters if a later pass tries to remove them. (2) The 'no other file covers these spawn GUIDs' claim is asserted, not searched. Cross notes and the automatic id check are both empty. I did not open the covering files because no removal depends on them.

answer.notes: Every test here drives the owned kart_pickups module directly and pins either captured golden bytes, refusals, persistence or respawn timing. The most similar file, kart_service.rs (shared score 46), exercises the same pickups only through the gateway (grant/destroy sequences at ~2791 and ~2892, pickup creation at ~2722 and ~2748, and an 'owned claim' path). It does not replace the unit-level assertions here, so nothing is marked superseded or duplicate. The only overlap is within the file (definitions_are_bounded_and_typed vs typed_items_accept_only_the_four_recovered_types). Lines 491-598 were not fully read; the respawn snapshot test was judged from its name, doc and the visible prefix. A reviewer could consider merging the two type tests, but that is a tidy-up, not a removal.

last_critiques.notes: No test is marked superseded, duplicate or obsolete, and whole_file_removable is false. Every verdict is keep, so no removal needs a covering test and the lens's replacement requirement is not triggered. The removal list is empty, so it can be wired as it stands. Two weaknesses lower the score but do not invalidate the audit. (1) The auditor admits it only read part of the respawn snapshot test (file lines 480-490 plus the excerpt), so that keep verdict rests on the test name and doc. It is a security-type check, so a full read before any future trimming is advisable. (2) The cross-file claims (kart_service.rs encode_expire(4) near line 1750, the grant/destroy sequences near lines 2791 and 2892, and the pickup creation near 2722 and 2748) were not verified in this pass. They only support the keep rationale, not any removal. The within-file overlap between definitions_are_bounded_and_typed and typed_items_accept_only_the_four_recovered_types is correctly kept.

answer.notes: I re-read the whole file and kart_review.rs. The previous answer's verdicts agree with the code for every test I checked. I did not read kart_review's checkpoint test body, so that verdict relies on the prior audit. Four tests stay as keep (malformed tunnels, duplicate delivery with serde round trip, laps/finish exact values, abandon-after-finish) and the identifiers test is kept conservatively, so the file is not wholly removable. problems.issue: Marked superseded by kart_review::restore_rejects_incoherent_snapshots_and_keeps_the_reward_schedule, but that test only covers snapshot-restore refusals. The five TrackLayout::new constructor refusals in this test (NoCheckpoints, ZeroCheckpoint, DuplicateCheckpoint(11), ZeroLaps, EmptyRewardSchedule) appear only in kart_racing.rs (grep of tests/ confirms no other use of these error variants). The restart test runs the same first claim, then a second claim expecting RewardError::Racing(KartRacingError::RewardAlreadyClaimed), and asserts coins and profile XP are unchanged. It adds a snapshot/serde round trip and reload before the second claim, and also asserts reward_claimed persists. All other verdicts are keeps and need no evidence. whole_file_removable=false is correct because the payout, refusal, rollback and wire-layout tests have no replacement. Minor caveat: the cover does not directly assert the live (non-restored) second-claim result, but the snapshot is taken from the same live session, so the live flag is still exercised before the snapshot. Cross-file overlap with kart_npc_entry.rs was not verified and is not needed for this removal.

Several keep reasons are therefore unverified, e.g. 'not reviewed against kart_pickups in detail', 'not clearly covered elsewhere', 'not reviewed against other files'. answer.notes: All twelve tests are unit-level codec, pose, lifecycle or refusal checks on src/kart_weapons.rs. The similar kart_service.rs tests exercise the service layer and assert subtypes and lengths, not per-field offsets, matrix values or forged-save fields, so none is clearly superseded. Nothing was obviously obsolete: the file's header says explosions and hits are deferred, and the current assertions match that. I did not compare against every similar file in depth, so a light overlap with kart_service.rs (the mine-use and pose-refusal paths) may exist, but no test here is a clear duplicate.

last_critiques.notes: The audit removes nothing: all twelve tests are marked keep, so no removal verdict needs a covering replacement. whole_file_removable=false is consistent with that. I spot-checked the two kart_service.rs claims the keeps rely on. weapon_pose_rejects_nan_invalid_basis_and_clock_regression (lines 265-287) covers only NaN, a zero basis and a clock regression at service level. It does not cover non-orthonormal, left-handed or future-stamp poses, so the unit pose test is not superseded. mine_use_emits_original_create_and_restores_bounded_lifecycle (lines 290-325) checks subtype 29 and length 84 and a restore plus expiry, but not matrix values or owner-local words, so the unit use_item test is not superseded either. The audit's confidence of 0.6 and its admission that it did not compare every similar file in depth are reasonable. The keep-all list is safe to hand to a builder, but it is not a real pruning review. Other kart_service tests were not checked for overlap.

The file's equality assertions overlap with tests/players_differential.rs, which is the strongest candidate for consolidation: registry_scaling's equality check could be dropped if the timing output is no longer needed. I did not read tests/multiplayer.rs or players_differential.rs in full, so the claim that no other test drives the 16-client UDP relay is based on search results only. The file's header notes that the W96 timing values are historical receipts, not live measurements.

Spot checks: the auditor's cited covering tests exist at tests/players_differential.rs:210 (dense_randomized_ordered_messages_match_reference) and :266 (cutoff_crossing_and_tie_canary_matches_reference). That is a note for later, not a defect in this audit. The auditor's confidence of 0.6 is honest, since it did not read multiplayer.rs or players_differential.rs in full.

answer.notes: Every test is kept. The pack's previous answer was truncated after test 14, so its verdicts for the later tests were not visible and I did not re-derive them in full. For the overlaps I checked, mining_lifecycle.rs and mining_review.rs drive different engines or assert different things, so no test is clearly superseded or duplicated. Confidence is low because I read only a few of the similar files. A deeper pass comparing assertions in mining_review.rs (reconnect/cancel, tamper, bounds) and mining_lifecycle.rs would be needed to remove anything.

problems.issue: The 'duplicate' verdict is not fully backed. tests/mining_review.rs::trailing_comma_is_tolerated_once_and_internal_empties_stay_invalid covers the chain path only: an internal empty and a double tail on OnChainMsg. The removed test also refuses the verify double tail 'OnVerifyMsg\t3,8,0,,' and checks state is unchanged. A grep for ',,' in mining_review.rs finds only the two OnChainMsg cases, so no other review test covers that refusal. Idle and single-tail verify acceptance are covered by native_client_chain_idle_and_verify_wire_text_is_accepted (lines 362-388), so those parts are duplicated.
problems.fix: Keep the test, or move the 'OnVerifyMsg\t3,8,0,,' refusal (with the state-unchanged check) into mining_review.rs before removing the mining.rs copy. Then re-verdict as duplicate.

problems.issue: The 'superseded' verdict holds. I read both bodies: mining_review's unusable_specs_are_rejected_at_load covers 601 refused, 600 accepted, shape codes (superset, including 499/699/800), 32x32 refused and the 448-cell tall board. duration_ceiling_matches_the_run_state_cap covers remaining_ms==600000.
problems.fix: keep the removal verdict as is, provided the builder is told the cited coverage is in mining_review.rs.

last_critiques.notes: Keep verdicts were not read in body for most tests. That is acceptable, since keeping is the safe direction, but the notes admit this. The whole_file_removable=false verdict is correct. The only removal with a coverage gap is the trailing-comma duplicate, which loses the verify double-tail refusal. Fix that before the list is wireable.

No test is marked superseded, duplicate or obsolete, and whole_file_removable is false, so no removal verdict needs a covering test. Keeping every test is the conservative outcome the lens allows, so the audit passes. The score is limited by weak work, not by a wrong removal. (1) Several keep reasons are only 'not checked against other files' or 'not confirmed elsewhere' (e.g. wildcard, collectable quota, idle gating, serde back-compat), so the audit did not establish uniqueness for those tests. (2) The auditor says it did not read the trailing-comma test in full and that the answer for tests 15 onward was truncated and not re-derived. (3) The audit's own confidence is 0.5. These gaps would matter if a later pass tries to prune this file, since the audit gives no evidence that any test is redundant. The list is wireable as is because it removes nothing. A follow-up pass that compares mining_review.rs (reconnect cancel, tamper, bounds, default spec) and mining_lifecycle.rs assertion by assertion would be needed before any removal.

problems.issue: All three verdicts are keep, so none is a removal and the evidence lens's replacement requirement does not apply. Each keep is conservative: the audit says no other test drives a bottom-row collectable through the chain-update or collect-update rebuild path, and the most similar file (mining_move_detection.rs) is named as not covering it. answer.notes: The pack's five most similar files (kart_service, housing_service, coin_store_siblings, npc_interaction, station_cash) are unrelated to Mining, so they yielded no overlap. Searching the repo showed no other test file that names OnPowerupInitMsg, TILE_POWERUP_* or the OnActionMsg powerup path. gathering_payout.rs:683 sends one t951 OnActionMsg, but it is a different gathering-payout path and not a duplicate. Other Type8Engine test files (mining.rs, mining_dead_board.rs, mining_move_detection.rs, mining_tile_rendering.rs) were not fully read; the lone-powerup HasMove test and the DEFAULT/no-key tests may overlap them. Within-file overlaps (dynamite, destruct and wildtile refusals) are noted but kept under the conservative rule. Stale comments: the RED comment on default_powerup_percent_matches... and the 'RED' on configured_collected_powerups... describe an earlier state.

last_critiques.notes: Every one of the 21 tests is verdicted keep, and whole_file_removable is false, so no removal is proposed and there is no unbacked removal to check against the lens. The 'only test of OnPowerupInitMsg' claim holds: a repo search finds OnPowerupInitMsg, TILE_POWERUP_* and validate_powerup_definitions referenced only in src/mining.rs, tests/mining_powerups.rs and notes. Residual weaknesses, none of which blocks handing the list to a builder: (1) the lone-powerup HasMove test and the default/no-key tests were not checked against tests/mining_move_detection.rs or mining_dead_board.rs, so their keep verdicts rest on an unverified 'only' claim; (2) the within-file overlaps (dynamite, wildtile refusals, destruct) are kept without comparison, which is safe under the conservative rule; (3) stale RED comments and dead cells.clear() code should be cleaned up as hygiene, not as removals; (4) shuffle_placement_walk partly recomputes expected values inside the test, which weakens it but does not justify removal. The audit is a safe keep-all result, not a reduction.

tests.name: shape1_regular_cells_exclude_collectables_at_forced_percent
tests.reason: Only test pinning the shape-1 (TILE_BUILDREGULAR) collectable-free pool at forced 100%. Other mining test files set collectable_percent to 0 (mining.rs, mining_dead_board.rs, mining_powerups.rs, mining_review.rs fixtures), so they never exercise the collectable pool and cannot cover this refusal.

tests.name: shape2_any_allows_collectables_at_forced_percent
tests.reason: Only check that shape 2 (TILE_BUILDANY) still draws collectables; no other test file drives the shape-to-pool dispatch with collectables enabled. Its positive assertion is the counterpart guarding against over-restriction.

tests.name: gravity_refill_queue_still_allows_collectables
tests.reason: Only test that checks the refill queue after a chain keeps the collectable-enabled pool (random_tile(true) path, src/mining.rs ~1539). Unique coverage of that path among the mining tests.

tests.name: mixed_seed_cases_keep_shape1_collectable_free
tests.reason: Different from the single-seed tests: it sweeps four seeds at 50% and asserts both the shape-1 refusal and a refill-queue assertion. Its shape-2 tail (seed 19, 100%) repeats shape2_any_allows_collectables_at_forced_percent with a different seed, so it is a partial overlap, but the multi-seed shape-1 sweep is not covered elsewhere. Kept conservatively.

answer.notes: The four tests are the only ones in the suite that set a non-zero collectable_percent and check the shape-to-pool dispatch in Type8 (mining.rs random_tile, shape codes 1/2). The similar files (mining_idle, mining_review, mining_move_detection, kart_service, quest_turnin_feedback) do not touch the collectable pool. The only possible trim is the trailing shape-2 block of mixed_seed_cases_keep_shape1_collectable_free, which duplicates shape2_any_allows_collectables_at_forced_percent with a different seed; I did not mark it removable. Fixtures are synthetic temp files and are cleaned up on drop.

last_critiques.notes: The audit proposes no removals: all four tests are marked keep, and whole_file_removable is false. Under the evidence lens, a keep verdict cannot remove coverage, so there are no removal verdicts to back and nothing blocks handing the list to a builder as it stands. I spot-checked the audit's main factual claim with a repo search. Other mining fixtures (mining.rs:119, mining_dead_board.rs:115, mining_powerups.rs:136, mining_review.rs:138, support/mining_quest_chain.rs:104) do set collectable_percent to 0, so the claim that they never exercise the collectable pool holds. The mining_review.rs:713 and mining.rs:812 hits assert a parsed value of 40 and do not drive the shape-to-pool dispatch, so they do not undercut the audit. The audit's own note that the trailing shape-2 block of mixed_seed_cases_keep_shape1_collectable_free partly overlaps shape2_any_allows_collectables_at_forced_percent is accurate. Keeping it is the conservative choice. Minor deduction only because the auditor's 'only test' claims were checked by search, not by reading every mining test body.

tests.name: initialize_board_sends_the_recovered_tile_index
tests.reason: Only test pinning Mining OnTileInfoMsg per-kind index (value - category) for the mining game. The similar OnTileInfoMsg checks in harvesting_tile_registration.rs, harvesting_runtime_tiles.rs and type8_native_repairs.rs drive other games' engines and tile sets, not this mining path.

tests.name: tile_index_never_underflows_on_malformed_content
tests.reason: Refusal check for hostile content (value below category). No other mining test asserts the 'below its category' error; mining_review.rs covers spec rejection at load but not this board-build refusal. Keep per refusal rule.

tests.name: tile_index_fix_keeps_run_state_and_snapshot_bytes
tests.reason: Persistence/canary check that the tile-index fix does not change run state or serialized snapshot bytes. mining.rs::serialized_state_round_trips_and_resumes_mid_run overlaps on round-trip but does not assert the 14x14 board length or the 401-405 tile presence after start-level, so it is not an equally strong substitute. Conservatively kept.

answer.notes: All three tests are short, targeted and mining-specific. The only partial overlap is the round-trip portion of the third test against tests/mining.rs. Consider merging the third test into a mining.rs snapshot test later, but no removal is warranted now.

last_critiques.notes: The audit proposes no removals: all three tests are marked keep and whole_file_removable is false, so the lens's removal-backing requirement does not apply. I checked the one factual claim the keep rationales rest on. The 'below its category' refusal is asserted only in tests/mining_tile_rendering.rs and is produced at src/mining.rs:1372, so the refusal test has no duplicate elsewhere in the repo. The 401-405 tile presence and 14x14 board length are asserted only in this file. The snapshot-bytes test's partial overlap with tests/mining.rs::serialized_state_round_trips_and_resumes_mid_run is real, and the audit's conservative keep is correct. The audit's suggestion to merge that third test later is not a removal and needs no action now.

tests.name: geoffrey_is_drawable_and_offers_the_missing_sisters
tests.reason: Only test pinning Geoffrey's 49/1 offer ids (intro/title/description 90621-90623) and the first-offer-no-duplicate rule for this quest. Its NpcVisibility AddNpc check overlaps partly with the spawn test below, but it is the only one that drives the Talk-to-offer path for 3000029. Could trim the spawn-field asserts as overlap, but not removable.

tests.name: the_search_visit_three_wolf_kills_and_final_talk_pay_once
tests.reason: Full happy-path chain for this quest (visit, three starter wolf kills, end screen, 49/14 XP to profile 1, job-switch no-pay). No other file drives Geoffrey's chain. Not a duplicate of local_hero_quest or blacksmith_first_order, which use different quests and NPCs.

tests.name: a_second_player_cannot_credit_or_pay_the_first
tests.reason: Cross-player isolation check (security-style: B's kills and turn-in must not credit or pay A). Similar tests exist in other quest files (local_hero_quest::a_second_player_killing_the_same_hooligans_does_not_advance_the_first, scavenger_hunt_quest::a_second_player_does_not_share_hunt_progress) but on different quests and content, so not equivalent. Keep.

tests.name: refusals_and_reconnect_change_nothing
tests.reason: Refusal test (wrong giver, out-of-range click, forged 49/2 and 49/14, out-of-radius visit) plus replayed 49/14 after reload. Refusal and persistence checks are kept by policy. The same-named test exists in blacksmith_first_order, medic_level_five_chapter and scavenger_hunt_quest, but each drives a different quest's refusals.

tests.name: the_spawn_is_unique_and_the_quest_target_resolves
tests.reason: Data canary: spawn GUID uniqueness, no content-key alias, Carlos neighbour row still present, quest target resolves to Geoffrey, and enabled-quest list at Geoffrey. Not covered elsewhere for this quest. Overlaps geoffrey_is_drawable on NpcVisibility, but the uniqueness and alias checks are unique.

tests.name: progress_survives_a_reconnect
tests.reason: Persistence check: one kill, save envelope, reload via game_store, progress intact. Persistence tests are kept by policy. Same-named tests in local_hero_quest and other files use different quest state and fixtures, so no equally strong duplicate is named.

tests.name: a_failing_quest_event_for_one_player_does_not_stop_the_other
tests.reason: Isolation/robustness check for a failing event on one player not blocking the other. Not read in full in this audit. Same-named tests exist in local_hero_quest, blacksmith_first_order and medic_level_five_chapter, but on different quests. Kept conservatively.

answer.notes: Every test here drives Geoffrey's quest 3000029 with its own content (spawn row, wolf group, reward bundle) and none is clearly duplicated in the five similar files. Those files share test names (refusals_and_reconnect_change_nothing, progress_survives_a_reconnect, a_failing_quest_event_for_one_player_does_not_stop_the_other, a_second_player_*) but test different quests, so they are template siblings, not duplicates. Only minor overlap: geoffrey_is_drawable and the_spawn_is_unique both check the NpcVisibility content key and spawn identity fields. Trimming those overlapping asserts is possible but low-value. I did not read the tail of the file (lines 860-1010: the rest of progress_survives_a_reconnect and the failing-event test body), so those two verdicts rest on names and the similar files, which lowers confidence.

last_critiques.notes: The audit proposes no removals: all seven tests are verdict keep, and whole_file_removable is false. The lens checks removal backing, so nothing needs a covering test. Keeping every test is the safe direction under the lens, so the list can go to a builder as a no-op. Two weaknesses are non-blocking. First, the audit says it did not read lines 860-1010, so the keep reasons for progress_survives_a_reconnect and a_failing_quest_event_for_one_player_does_not_stop_the_other rest on test names and sibling files. A later removal pass on this file should read that tail first. Second, geoffrey_is_drawable and the_spawn_is_unique overlap on NpcVisibility and spawn identity. The audit correctly flags this as a possible trim, not a removal. Score is held to 8 because of the unread tail and the low audit confidence (0.6).

tests.name: riders_are_seen_by_neighbours_and_late_arrivals_and_a_mounted_emote_is_dropped
tests.reason: Socket-level end-to-end run (gateway + bots) of summon, refusal of an unowned ride, boarding seen by a neighbour, mounted emote drop, late arrival seeing the ride, dismount removing it for all, and removal on leave. tests/mount_routing.rs covers the same rules at unit level (an_owned_ride_is_summoned_boarded_and_put_away, a_ride_the_player_does_not_own_is_refused, a_mounted_rider_cannot_emote, a_second_player_in_range_sees_the_ride_and_its_removal), but none of them exercises the wire, the gateway debounce or a late joiner. Only partial overlap, so kept.

tests.name: the_ride_moves_with_its_rider_and_a_late_arrival_gets_the_native_mount_tail
tests.reason: Only socket-level check that a ride follows its rider's moves and that a late arrival's AddPc carries the native mount block (guid, seat, queue position, lift) and then the ride actor. mount_routing.rs has a_seated_rider_carries_the_mount_tail_and_the_ride_copies_its_moves at unit level, which is the closest equivalent; the wire-byte assertions here are not shown to be duplicated. Kept, with the caveat that the unit test may cover the same tail bytes.

answer.notes: The file has only two #[test] functions (lines 613 and 715). Both are end-to-end and mostly exercise paths that mount_routing.rs tests in-process, so the overlap is partial rather than a duplicate. I did not read mount_routing.rs past line 300 or mount_stats.rs, so I did not confirm whether mount_routing's tail/move test asserts the same bytes. The rig is copied from bot_acceptance_1016.rs (shared rig code, not duplicate tests). Both tests take about 20 s of socket time each; if suite time matters, the first one's unowned-refusal and emote-drop checks could be moved to mount_routing, but that would lose the wire coverage, so I did not recommend removal.

problems.issue: The keep reason is hedged ("the wire-byte assertions here are not shown to be duplicated"; "the unit test may cover the same tail bytes"). I checked mount_routing.rs:396-446: a_seated_rider_carries_the_mount_tail_and_the_ride_copies_its_moves asserts the MountTail struct, the Mount response fields at offsets 19/23/27/35, and the follow-copy bytes. It does not assert the late-arrival AddPc mount block on the wire, and the bot test's late-arrival check is not covered there. So the keep is right, but the reason should state that instead of hedging.
problems.fix: keep it (tighten the reason: the unit test covers the Mount response and follow bytes but not the late-arrival AddPc tail on the wire)

problems.issue: Keep is correct. The auditor's named unit overlaps are partial: they do not exercise the socket wire, gateway debounce, or a late joiner. No removal is claimed.

last_critiques.notes: Both verdicts are keep and whole_file_removable is false, so no removal verdict needed backing. The lens's removal checks therefore have nothing to reject. I confirmed the one covering unit test I opened does not replace the wire-level late-arrival AddPc check. The auditor's confidence of 0.6 is fair given it did not read mount_routing past line 300 or mount_stats.rs. Consider a follow-up reading players.rs add_pc tests if anyone later proposes trimming this file.

tests.name: an_unmounted_player_keeps_the_sentinel_tail
tests.reason: Only test that pins the AddPc tail bytes of an unmounted player (sentinel guid 0, seat -1, queue -1) through PlayerRegistry::join. tests/mount_routing.rs checks MountService::view().tail() (the service value), not the bytes players.rs writes into AddPc, so it does not cover this path.

tests.name: a_viewer_who_arrives_later_gets_the_riders_mount_block
tests.reason: Only check that a late viewer's AddPc carries the rider's ride GUID, seat, queue and lift, and that the frame size and the other bytes are unchanged. The similar mount_routing test a_seated_rider_carries_the_mount_tail_and_the_ride_copies_its_moves asserts the service-side tail and the 168/2 Mount response, not the AddPc frame built in players.rs, so it is not a duplicate.

tests.name: setting_a_mount_sends_nothing_and_clearing_it_restores_the_sentinel
tests.reason: Covers that set_mount emits no packets, that the seated tail survives a leave-and-return of the rider, that clearing with MountTail::NONE restores the plain AddPc, and that an unknown session is ignored. No other file drives set_mount on the registry. The unknown-session check is weak on its own but is part of a unique path, so it is kept.

answer.notes: The five most similar files (housing_session, power_up_drops, fishing_entry, coin_store_siblings, sc_earnings) contain no mount tests and were not overlapping. The closest is tests/mount_routing.rs (a_seated_rider_carries_the_mount_tail_and_the_ride_copies_its_moves), which checks MountService and the Mount response rather than the players.rs AddPc bytes. tests/mount_stats.rs and tests/mount_roster.rs also use MountService, not PlayerRegistry::set_mount. Confidence is limited by not having read every mount file in full.

last_critiques.notes: The audit proposes no removals: all three tests in tests/mount_follow.rs are marked keep, covered_by is null for each, and whole_file_removable is false. The lens checks for superseded, duplicate or obsolete verdicts therefore have nothing to test, and keeping every test is the safe outcome. I confirmed the one named neighbour exists: tests/mount_routing.rs:396 a_seated_rider_carries_the_mount_tail_and_the_ride_copies_its_moves. The audit's claim that it asserts service-side tail() rather than the players.rs AddPc bytes is consistent with the code I could see, but I did not read that test body, so that distinction is unverified. The reasoning for keeping is plausible and the risk is one-sided. The score is docked because the audit did not read every mount file and it cites no equivalent check for the unknown-session line in the third test, which it calls weak. Cross notes against quest answers were empty, and the automatic id check was empty.

tests.name: world_entry_sends_the_owned_ride_roster
tests.reason: Only test pinning the exact 168/5 world-entry row bytes (fields, 53/5 pet roster beside it, empty roster with no rides). tests/mount_bots.rs only waits for a 168/5 prefix end-to-end and does not decode rows.

tests.name: grants_send_the_roster_once_and_nothing_else_does
tests.reason: Guards exactly-once roster per ride change and that non-ride grants, repeat grants and idle ticks send nothing. No other file in the compared set asserts this no-duplicate behaviour.

tests.name: summon_put_away_and_refusal_rosters_leave_nothing_for_the_sync
tests.reason: Covers summon, put-away and refused-summon rosters and asserts the following settle adds no second roster; includes a refusal check. tests/mount_stats.rs and tests/mount_wired.rs exercise settle_mounts but assert owner updates and 168/4 or 35/3 removal packets, not these 168/5 roster contents.

tests.name: a_new_session_sends_the_roster_again_at_world_entry_and_nothing_before
tests.reason: Pins the new-session resend and absence of any roster before world entry; not found in the compared files.

tests.name: losing_the_ride_item_puts_the_ride_away
tests.reason: Previous duplicate verdict not confirmed. tests/mount_stats.rs (around lines 282-291) drives the same trade-away path but asserts only owner_updates equals the restored effect; it does not check the removes_ride 35/3 packet count in nearby or the absence of a 168/5 roster, which this test asserts. Partial overlap only, so kept conservatively.

tests.name: a_scaled_dragon_stays_out_while_another_of_its_items_is_owned
tests.reason: Service-level multi-item ownership check (ride stays while a sibling item is owned, put away exactly once when the last is gone) using the real mounts.json catalogue; refusal-style guard not reproduced in the similar files. Not fully read beyond lines 311-345, but the assertions are specific.

answer.notes: Similar-file scan (mount_stats, mount_wired, mount_bots, mount_routing) shows overlapping setup and settle_mounts calls but different assertions on the packets. Earlier low-confidence duplicate verdict for losing_the_ride_item was reversed after reading mount_stats.rs. Lines 1-300 of the file were judged from the excerpt and prior answer rather than re-read in full.

problems.issue: The verdict 'duplicate' of losing_the_ride_item_puts_the_ride_away is not backed. The covering block in mount_stats.rs (lines 282-291) only runs the trade-away and checks that owner_updates equals `restored`. It does not check the 168/5 roster rows, the (BAT,0) remaining-ride assertion, the observer despawn count, the 168/4 dismount count, the no-active-guid state, or the following tick being silent. It also covers only the Wolf item, with no mounted/unmounted loop. The auditor's own note says the match was not verified line by line, and it is not a same-path, at-least-as-strong match.

The Lava Tiger block inside this test is a refusal ('another owned candidate item keeps it out: nothing is sent'). It asserts that no 168 packet is sent after a trade-away of one of two candidate items, in both mounted states. Nothing in mount_stats.rs or elsewhere in the compared set covers the two-item Lava Tiger case, so under the lens it needs an equally strong named replacement before any removal.

The other keep verdicts are unverified. The auditor says it checked only grep hits and call sites in mount_wired, mount_stats, mounts and mount_routing, not their full assertions. The 'no other file checks this' claims for the roster bytes, the once-per-change guard and the new-session resend rest on that partial read.
Correctly false. The only removal candidate is not backed, so the removal list is empty and nothing is wireable as a removal.

last_critiques.notes: Only one removal candidate exists, and the lens does not support it. Keep the whole file. The auditor's confidence of 0.5 is fair. Before any removal, read mount_stats.rs and mount_wired.rs in full and check their assertions against this file's roster-byte and observer checks.

problems.issue: a_scaled_dragon_stays_out_while_another_of_its_items_is_owned is kept on a partly read file (the auditor says it read only lines 311-345). The keep is conservative and no removal rests on it, so this is a gap in the evidence rather than an error in the verdict.
The claim that tests/mount_bots.rs only waits for a 168/5 prefix and does not decode rows is asserted, not shown. It does not change the keep verdict, since a keep needs no proof of uniqueness.
The losing_the_ride_item reason first states a duplicate verdict, then reverses it. The final keep is supported by the partial overlap with mount_stats.rs, and the reversal is recorded in the reason.

last_critiques.notes: Every verdict in the answer is keep, and whole_file_removable is false, so no removal is proposed. The lens checks removal verdicts, and none exist, so there is no removal to back and nothing that could drop a only-check. The keeps are the safe direction. The answer is honest about its limits: confidence 0.6, lines 1-300 judged from an excerpt, and an earlier duplicate verdict reversed. Cross notes and the id check are empty. The file as a whole is retained, and the removal list is trivially wireable. Score is lowered only for the incomplete reading and the unverified similar-file claims.

tests.name: request_bodies_are_decoded_strictly
tests.reason: Hostile-input decoder canary: truncated, padded and oversized bodies must error, and non-request families must decode to None. No similar file asserts decoder strictness directly.

tests.name: an_owned_ride_is_summoned_boarded_and_put_away
tests.reason: Changed from superseded. mount_wired.rs (the gameplay-level twin) only drives the 168/6 spawn, 168/1 board and 168/3 put-away; it does not send the 168/8 item-path summon that this test also asserts. mount_wired also does not compile until the lead-owned shared patch is applied, so it cannot yet be the sole replacement. The 38/7 owner-only stat block is covered by tests/mount_stats.rs::boarding_sends_the_ride_stat_block_to_the_owner_only, and the byte layouts by tests/mounts.rs::spawn_mount_dismount_then_despawn_have_expected_bytes_and_fanout. Remove only after the 168/8 item-path summon and the wire-level put-away are asserted in a compiling test.

tests.name: a_ride_the_player_does_not_own_is_refused
tests.reason: Refusal check with hostile input: unknown ride id -1, unknown item id, and a 168/1 naming another actor boards nothing. mount_wired::a_ride_the_player_does_not_own_is_refused_with_a_notice and mounts.rs::unowned_mount_is_rejected cover only the basic refusal.

tests.name: restrictions_block_summoning_and_boarding
tests.reason: mounts.rs::restrictions_reject_spawn_in_minigame_ability_or_blocked_zone checks only the service-level Err(Restricted). This test also pins the wire-level refusal notice for minigame, ability and zone, which mount_wired does not cover (its only refusal check is the knockout case). Removing it would leave the wire refusal untested.

tests.name: every_server_trigger_dismounts_and_removes_the_ride
tests.reason: Partial overlap only. mount_wired covers knockout, chasing enemy, instance battle and zoning at gameplay level. Minigame and ability endings are checked only at service level in mounts.rs::minigame_and_ability_start_remove_the_ride, which does not drive the gameplay trigger path. Not removable until those endings are asserted through the trigger path in a compiling test.

tests.name: a_second_player_in_range_sees_the_ride_and_its_removal
tests.reason: Checks interest-range fanout, late-joiner replay of the ride actor and attachment, and the removal packet for others. No similar file replays the view to a late joiner.

tests.name: a_seated_rider_carries_the_mount_tail_and_the_ride_copies_its_moves
tests.reason: W167 behaviour: AddPc mount tail fields and the ride copying only the rider's position updates, rejecting other players, families and short packets. Unique among the similar files.

tests.name: a_mounted_rider_cannot_emote
tests.reason: Refusal gate: emote_context().mounted refuses EmoteRejection::Mounted while riding and allows it after dismount. mount_wired checks the mounted flag at gateway level but not the EmoteRejection outcome, so it is not a full duplicate.

tests.name: every_catalogued_ride_builds_a_valid_actor
tests.reason: Catalogue-wide canary: every shipped mount summons with no notice and a valid 35/2 AddNpc. mounts.rs::client_table_and_mount_data_load_with_provenance only counts rows.

tests.name: effects_keep_the_owner_roster_private
tests.reason: Privacy check: the owner roster effect is non-nearby and the ride actor effect is nearby. The mounts.rs fanout test checks recipients but not the nearby flag.

answer.notes: No test is removable with confidence. The only earlier removal candidate (an_owned_ride_is_summoned_boarded_and_put_away) is kept because mount_wired.rs does not exercise the 168/8 item-path summon, and mount_wired itself does not compile until the lead-owned shared patch lands, so it cannot be relied on yet. Revisit once mount_wired compiles and the item-path summon is covered there or in mounts.rs at wire level. The previous 'superseded' verdict was overstated. mount_stats.rs was checked only for its boarding test name and marketplace_owned_rides.rs was not read; neither changes the verdicts above.

problems.issue: Marked superseded, but the named cover (mount_wired.rs::an_owned_ride_is_summoned_boarded_and_put_away_through_gameplay) does not assert the 168/8 item-path summon, which the audit itself calls an extra. I read mount_wired lines 1-300: it only uses the 168/6 spawn path. The 38/7 owner-only block is probably covered by mount_stats::boarding_sends_the_ride_stat_block_to_the_owner_only, but I did not open that file to confirm it. The audit's own note says to move the item-path check before deleting, so the verdict contradicts its own reason.
problems.fix: keep it until the 168/8 item-path summon is moved into mount_wired or mounts.rs at wire level, then re-verdict.

problems.issue: Covered_by mounts.rs::restrictions_reject_spawn_in_minigame_ability_or_blocked_zone, which I read. It checks only service.spawn returning Err(Restricted) and does not drive the wire path. The gateway/handler mapping of Restricted to a refusal notice is what this test checks, and it covers the minigame, ability and zone contexts. mount_wired's only refusal check is the knockout case (lines 177-179). So the wire-level refusal for minigame, ability and blocked zone would be left with no test. The audit's 'weak UI string' framing understates this.
problems.fix: keep it, or first add a wire-level refusal test (notice, no 35/2 for minigame, ability and zone) to mount_wired and then remove this one.

problems.issue: Covered_by names only mount_wired, which covers knockout, chasing enemy, instance battle and zoning (lines 163-216). The minigame and ability endings are not in mount_wired, and the audit concedes they live in mounts.rs::minigame_and_ability_start_remove_the_ride. That test is service-level, and I read it: it asserts the 168/4 reply and DespawnRide effect, but it does not go through the gameplay trigger path. The gameplay-level minigame and ability endings therefore have no wire-level cover. Calling this 'duplicate' overstates the coverage.
problems.fix: keep it, or split the verdict: remove only the parts proven covered by mount_wired, and keep the minigame and ability ending until a gameplay-level test exists.

problems.issue: Correctly false, but the removal list depends on mount_wired.rs, which does not compile until lead-owned shared patch lands (its header says so). Removing tests whose only replacement is in a non-compiling file would leave no working check in the tree.
problems.fix: Do not hand off any superseded removals until mount_wired.rs compiles in the tree, or keep all three candidates.

problems.issue: Verdict is keep, and the reason is sound: the hostile 168/1 and bad-id cases are not in mount_wired or mounts.rs. Confirmed.

Verdict is keep, and correct. mount_wired's gateway test (lines 9-10, 241-242) says the emote refusal itself is covered in tests/mount_routing.rs, so this test is the only one for authorize_emote refusal. The audit's 'not read, so keep to be safe' is the right call.

last_critiques.notes: The audit ran the right overlap checks at test-name level but did not verify that each covering test drives the same path with at least as much assertion. Of the three removal candidates, none is safe to remove as stated: each has an extra the audit itself flagged, or a wire-level refusal or ending that has no other cover. Keep verdicts for request decoding, the unowned refusal, the late-joiner fanout, the W167 tail, the emote gate, the catalogue canary and the privacy check look sound. I did not read mount_stats.rs or the mount_wired gateway test body past line 295, which would be needed to fully confirm the 38/7 and emote claims.

problems.issue: Verdict 'superseded' by mount_wired::an_owned_ride_is_summoned_boarded_and_put_away_through_gameplay is not backed. Checked mount_wired.rs lines 113-143: the owned test summons only via spawn() (168/6) and boards via board(); it never sends the 168/8 item request for an owned ride. The 168/8 request appears in mount_wired only in the refusal test (line 150). So the removed test's wire-level assertion that an owned item-path summon succeeds (by_item.shared.len()==1, view present) has no wire-level replacement; mounts.rs::item_definition_spawn_uses_the_catalog_crosswalk is service-level only. tests.reason: Only test in the file. It is a packet-driven, gateway-level run of all 17 opening stages (talk/interact, dungeon select and kills, win, restart, return to zone 0). It also carries refusal checks: a remote interaction with the guide and with the magic door must leave the snapshot unchanged, and a forged/remote entrance cannot zone the player. Those refusal and persistence assertions (coins and position survive restart) are not clearly matched by opening.rs::private_opening_every_stage_is_completable_through_typed_events_and_reward_once_after_reload, which works at the engine level with typed events rather than through the gateway packet path. Since it is ignored and needs private content, it adds no per-run cost unless the env vars are set.

answer.notes: The pack lists a single test. Similar opening tests in tests/opening.rs (private_opening_every_stage_is_completable_through_typed_events_and_reward_once_after_reload, private_opening_content_loads_with_all_objectives_and_verified_actor_references) overlap the stage-completion and reward-once path but at the engine level, not through Gateway packets. The gateway-specific refusal checks are the reason to keep. Confidence is moderate because I did not read the full opening.rs assertions side by side with this file; if that comparison shows the stage loop is identical, the stage-walk portion could be judged superseded, but the refusal and restart checks would still need keeping.

last_critiques.notes: The audit makes no removal verdicts. Its single test, private_all_opening_actions_dungeon_return_and_restarts, is marked keep, and whole_file_removable is false, so the lens's superseded/duplicate checks do not apply and no removal needs a named replacement. The keep is the conservative direction under the lens, since the test carries refusal checks (remote guide and magic-door interactions leaving the snapshot unchanged, forged entrance not zoning) and restart persistence checks (coins and position). The audit's own confidence is 0.6 because it did not compare the stage loop against tests/opening.rs side by side. That gap only affects whether the stage-walk portion could be trimmed later, not this verdict. Optional follow-up: if anyone later wants to remove the stage loop, the refusal and restart assertions must be carried into a gateway-level test first.

problems.issue: Marked superseded by tests/emotes.rs::mounted_actors_cannot_emote_but_can_still_use_plain_chat. The mounted and moving refusals are genuinely covered there: that test loops over every EMOTE_ACTIONS row through the catalog wrapper for Mounted, and moving_blocks_only_the_freeze_movement_slot covers outfitall Moving{3001}. But the removed test also asserts the returned animation ids from validate_emote: wave=3354, cheer=3306, dance=3200 (lines 216-219, 237, 246-247). emotes.rs::every_recovered_emote_is_accepted_standing only asserts Ok/refused lists, not the resolved animation id, and the rows test in piece_093 checks ids for 138, 168, 175, 2472, 2486 but not 143 (wave), 3306 (cheer) or 184's returned 3200 through validate. So the claim that emotes.rs has 'equal or stronger checks across every recovered row' is not accurate for the animation-id assertions. The stated reason is also hedged ('could be dropped if the direct API is not needed'), which is not a firm removal backing.
problems.fix: keep it (or split it: keep the wave/cheer/dance animation-id asserts, e.g. as a standalone test, and only drop the mounted/moving refusal lines that emotes.rs already covers). Do not remove the whole test as superseded.

The unverified module-path note about osfr_tools::social_chat::piece_093 is not load-bearing: social_chat.rs:472 calls piece_093::validate_emote_phrase, so the path is in use. Confidence moderate; I did not open the rest of emotes.rs (lines 170-374) beyond what the verdict needed.

All nine tests are marked keep and whole_file_removable is false, so no removal is made that needs a replacement. tests.name: the_same_kill_id_in_two_instances_heals_each_group_once
tests.reason: Unique check that the instance is part of the kill identity (same guid+ms in a child instance is a separate kill). Nothing elsewhere asserts this; it guards cross-instance isolation.

tests.name: a_picker_without_a_committed_place_claims_nothing

tests.name: the_memory_is_bounded

answer.notes: Small, focused file testing the World-level group-heal ledger directly. Similar files (power_up_drops.rs) test the same feature end-to-end via tick/drop rather than claim_group_heal itself; their overlap is partial (different layer), so nothing is marked superseded. No test here is redundant.

last_critiques.notes: All four tests are marked keep, with no superseded, duplicate or obsolete verdicts, and whole_file_removable is false. The evidence lens only requires backing for removal verdicts, so there is nothing here that needs a covering test. The keep reasons are plausible against the evidence pack. The World-level claim_group_heal ledger is exercised directly, and power_up_drops::big_hearts_from_one_kill_share_a_kill_key_so_the_group_heals_once is listed in the pack as testing the tick/drop layer rather than the ledger. The instance-scoped kill identity, the refused-claim-consumes-nothing rule and the 256-entry bound each have no equivalent in the listed similar files. Only minor gap: the audit's confidence is 0.8, and I did not open power_up_drops.rs to confirm the big-heart test's assertions. That does not change the outcome, because no removal depends on it.

tests.name: shipped_file_loads_and_references_resolve
tests.reason: Only check that the shipped power_ups.json loads and exposes the standard/elite/boss tables and the flame_wave/energy kinds with the expected auto flags; the similar power_up_drops.rs tests exercise the engine, not this module-level load.

tests.name: every_bound_rejects_a_bad_file

tests.name: non_finite_and_unknown_fields_and_oversize_are_rejected
tests.reason: Hostile-input refusal: NaN-as-string, unknown field, oversize document, and malformed JSON. Security/refusal check, so kept.

tests.name: roll_is_deterministic_for_a_fixed_seed
tests.reason: Pins the splitmix64 output for seed 0 as a generator canary and checks seeded reproducibility. No other file pins this value.

tests.name: roll_distribution_matches_chances_and_weights
tests.reason: Statistical check of drop rate and pool weights over 400k rolls at the module level. power_up_drops.rs has a group-multiplier sample but not this per-weight share check. Costly but not a duplicate; possible candidate to shrink, not to remove.

tests.name: zero_chance_never_drops

The distribution test is the slowest (400k rolls) and could be sped up, but it is not redundant. Nothing in this file is clearly obsolete: no later task replaced its behaviour, and the file has no creator or changer recorded in the pack.

last_critiques.notes: The audit proposes no removals: all seven tests are marked keep, so no superseded, duplicate or obsolete verdict needs a covering test. whole_file_removable=false is correct. I checked the one factual claim that carries weight: the pinned splitmix64 value 0xe220_a839_7b1d_cdaf appears only in tests/power_ups.rs, so the 'no other file pins this value' claim holds. power_up_drops.rs line 88 does use chance 0.0, but only in a fixture, so the zero_chance_never_drops keep is not clearly undermined. Weaknesses: the auditor did not read power_up_drops.rs in full, and its claim that the engine-level guaranteed tests are about boss content, not roll ordering, is unverified. Confidence 0.5 reflects that. The 'shrink the distribution test' remark is a suggestion, not a verdict, so it does not affect the removal list. Keeping everything is the conservative choice the lens favours.

tests.name: every_priced_vendor_is_drawable

tests.name: a_far_or_wrong_zone_click_changes_nothing

tests.name: two_players_see_and_open_the_same_vendor

tests.name: a_reconnect_keeps_the_vendor_drawable_and_shop_openable

answer.notes: All five tests are the only checks of the T372 priced-vendor content guard, the Florina/Fladnag drawability and shop routes, or the reconnect persistence path. Overlap exists with tests/npc_interaction.rs (vendor menu, 165/10 layout, 26/8-26/10 routing, two-session refusal), so the refusal and two-session tests are the best candidates for future trimming if a stronger equivalent is confirmed. I did not read npc_interaction.rs bodies in full, so the overlap judgement is based on test names only. The file also depends on lab/ report files and the reconstructed spawn data; if those are absent the tests fail rather than pass vacuously.

last_critiques.notes: The audit proposes no removals: all five tests are marked keep, covered_by is null throughout, and whole_file_removable is false. The keep verdicts are the conservative choice and no removal is backed or needed, so nothing in the removal list can cause a lost check. Two caveats do not change the verdict. First, the overlap claims for tests 2, 3 and 4 against tests/npc_interaction.rs rest on test names only; the auditor says it did not read those bodies. That matters only if a later pass wants to trim, so before any future removal that file should be read and the named replacements checked for equal strength. Second, the file depends on lab/ reports and reconstructed spawn data; if they are missing the tests fail rather than pass vacuously, which is a fragility to note, not a reason to remove anything. The auditor's notes are accurate about these limits.

tests.name: class_unlock_selection_activation_and_restart_retain_equipment

tests.reason: Asserts unowned bytes are preserved across gender/class splices and that unproved input is refused. Refusal plus byte-preservation; keep.

tests.name: private_all_opening_starters_and_fresh_identity_survive_activation_and_restore

Exercises the full starter/activation/restore/identity-refusal chain across all opening classes; opening_gateway.rs private test covers gateway flow, not this profile-level chain. Keep; not verifiable as duplicate without private files.

tests.name: class_selection_without_class_content_is_refused_and_keeps_the_save
tests.reason: Regression guard for a panic (c90ed46 review blocker 3) on a contentless pack; asserts silent refusal and unchanged snapshot. Canary/refusal check; nothing equivalent found elsewhere.

answer.notes: Every test here is a profile-specific check (class unlock/select, XP overflow and packet layout, snapshot refusal, proof corruption, gender/class splice byte preservation, a private-content chain, and a contentless-pack regression guard). Searching the repo for the same functions (add_experience, patch_self on profiles, stage_job_selection, class selection) found only the other profile-adjacent files (kart_rewards.rs, l052_staff_jobs.rs, opening_journal.rs, quests.rs) that exercise different engines (kart rewards, staff jobs, journal, quest templates), not profile selection or XP packets. The five similar files (housing_service, piece_032, npc_interaction, inventory, login) share vocabulary but not these paths. Nothing removable; the one ignored private test depends on OSFR_OPENING_CONTENT and was not run here.

last_critiques.notes: All eight tests in tests/profiles.rs are verdicted keep, with covered_by null, and whole_file_removable is false. Under the evidence lens, no removal verdict exists that needs backing, so no covering test had to be opened. Keeping is the safe direction: the audit's refusal, persistence, canary and packet-layout checks (class lock refusal, XP overflow no-op, snapshot refusal, proof corruption, unowned-byte preservation, contentless-pack panic regression) are the kind of checks the brief says must not be dropped without an equally strong replacement. The audit's 'no equivalent elsewhere' claims are weaker than a removal would need, but they only matter if something is removed, and nothing is. Residual risk: the ignored private test (OSFR_OPENING_CONTENT) was not run, so its uniqueness is asserted, not verified. The removal list is empty, so it is wireable as is. Confidence in the audit is reduced only by the unverified 'no duplicate elsewhere' reasoning, which does not change any action.

tests.name: add_entry_body_matches_client_reader_8d8570

tests.name: source_content_ids_are_unique_and_locale_backed

tests.name: shipped_achievement_rules_join_every_title_by_name
tests.reason: Pins the shipped rule/title/claim binding counts and the job slug from the real data files. Canary-type check; keep.

answer.notes: No test is clearly redundant. The closest overlaps are titles_claims.rs (claim and title-select flows through the gateway) and progression_extras_content.rs (content id resolution). Those are end-to-end or partial overlaps, and each test here adds assertions they lack, so all are kept under the conservative rule. piece_038.rs drives a #[path] copy of a different module, so it is not the same path. This file has no shared helpers or crate modules beyond osfr_tools, and it was last changed by T229, which did not obsolete any test here. I did not read the shipped src/progression_extras.rs, so the claims about exact assertion equivalence rest on test bodies and names only.

last_critiques.notes: The audit marks all 14 tests keep and whole_file_removable false. No removal verdict exists, so there is no removal to back with a covering test, and the evidence lens is satisfied. Keeping is the conservative outcome under the rule that a redundant test is cheaper than a lost check. The removal list is empty, so it can be handed to a builder as it stands. Weaknesses that do not change the outcome: several keep reasons assert 'not covered elsewhere' or 'not asserted in the other files' (remove_body_is_one_collection_id, completing_with_an_empty_grant_sends_no_reward_toast, failed_definition_lookup_does_not_leave_a_claim_tracker) without checking the other files. The auditor also admits it did not read src/progression_extras.rs, so its equivalence claims rest on test names and bodies only. Those gaps would matter only if a later pass tried to remove these tests.

tests.name: title_and_collection_ids_resolve_to_client_data
