The overlapping parts (count of 90 titles and 241 collections, client_id uniqueness, locale ids non-empty) are also asserted in tests/progression_extras.rs::source_content_ids_are_unique_and_locale_backed, but that test does not check images or item definitions, so this one is not clearly covered elsewhere.

answer.notes: Single-test file. Partial overlap with progression_extras.rs::source_content_ids_are_unique_and_locale_backed (counts, id uniqueness, locale resolution via assert_locale_ids_resolve) and with progression_extras.rs::shipped_achievement_rules_join_every_title_by_name (title count 90). Its unique value is the client-data cross-check (images, item definitions) and the Briarwood fixture. Could trim the duplicated count/locale asserts if the suite cost matters, but the file as a whole should stay. Reads lab/ reference files, so it depends on the lab checkout being present.

last_critiques.notes: The audit's only verdict is keep, with whole_file_removable false, so there is no removal to back and nothing in the evidence lens is violated. The keep is defensible. The audit says the image and item-definition cross-checks are unique to this test. A search of prototype/osfr-tools/tests found no other test that checks title image_id against Images.txt. The Briarwood check (17054, category 3) overlaps partly with collection_catalogue.rs, which asserts (name_id, category_id) == (17054, 3), but that test does not check the image or item-definition resolution. I did not open progression_extras.rs to confirm its source_content_ids test lacks image checks, so that claim is taken from the audit. The notes suggest trimming duplicated count and locale asserts, but no removal was recommended, so no change is needed. The file depends on the lab/ checkout, which the audit flags correctly.

tests.name: the_shipped_crosswalk_loads_and_points_at_real_quests
tests.reason: Only test that checks the shipped data/content/breadcrumb_quests.json against the real quest catalogue (ids exist, no id-space overlap, Cooking starter reachable, unsupported mappings stay unavailable). Data canary.

tests.name: every_shipped_row_names_its_points_and_says_how_it_was_decided
tests.reason: Provenance invariant on the shipped file (legacy-data and client sources, (R) tag on reconstructed decisions). Nothing else reads these tags.

tests.name: a_missing_file_is_an_empty_crosswalk
tests.reason: Loader contract for an absent file; no other test calls load_crosswalk on a missing file.

tests.name: unmapped_rows_are_kept_out_of_the_map
tests.reason: Loader behaviour for regional_quest_id null; unique to this file.

tests.name: malformed_crosswalks_are_errors_not_silent_empties
tests.reason: Refusal and hostile-input check across many malformed documents; no equivalent elsewhere.

tests.name: only_breadcrumb_starts_are_rewritten
tests.reason: Checks translate() passes Select and Lock through untouched and only rewrites Breadcrumb; no other test calls translate directly.

tests.name: a_listed_original_id_offers_its_regional_quest_once
tests.reason: Offer path (single offer, Offered status, no award, re-press re-shows the same offer, accept to Active with zero counts) is asserted at equal or greater strength in quest_journal. The only extra step here is the 1807->10 translate mapping, which the loader tests above already pin.

tests.name: an_unlisted_original_id_is_refused_and_changes_nothing
tests.reason: Refusal check for original ids absent from the crosswalk (1814) and for forged values; translate returns None so nothing reaches the journal. quest_journal only covers regional or forged ids sent as breadcrumbs directly, not the unmapped-original gate.

tests.name: a_listed_id_the_engine_will_not_offer_is_refused_with_a_denial_and_changes_nothing
tests.reason: Same denials (Prerequisite for 11, Unavailable for hollow 12, Level for 13), same no-change and no-award assertions, driven through the same journal handler. The translate step only maps 1808/1809/1810 to 11/12/13.

tests.name: a_full_quest_log_refuses_the_start_and_says_so
tests.reason: Same Limit denial, same QuestLimit{member:true} notice, same state-unchanged assertion. Only difference is how the slot is filled (offer+accept of 15 here, activate 14 there).

tests.name: a_listed_id_for_a_quest_already_done_or_held_changes_nothing
tests.reason: Active-quest breadcrumb only selects, no award, and a repeat press changes nothing; quest_journal asserts the same. The completed-quest refusal is covered by quest_journal::breadcrumb_cannot_be_used_to_skip_an_open_offer_or_finished_quest.

answer.notes: Six of eleven tests are the gateway-shaped journal checks, which quest_journal.rs already covers at equal or greater strength; they could be dropped without loss, though the translate step is their only extra coverage. The loader, shipped-data and provenance tests (about half the file) are unique and should be kept, so the file as a whole is not removable. I did not re-verify the quest_journal assertions beyond reading them, and the previous answer's truncated reasoning was not re-checked.

problems.issue: Marked superseded by quest_journal::breadcrumb_makes_the_normal_offer_and_never_completes_anything, but that test calls crumb(10) with the regional id directly and never goes through translate(). This file's start() helper runs translate(1807 -> 10) first, so the original-to-regional step is the path under test and the covering test does not exercise it. The verdict's claim that the translate step is covered by the file's own loader/translate tests is also weak: only_breadcrumb_starts_are_rewritten uses a synthetic map and checks only that Select/Lock are untouched, not the 1807 start.

Marked duplicate of quest_journal::breadcrumb_refusals_leave_state_untouched, which passes regional ids 11, 12, 13 straight to the engine. This test passes originals 1808, 1809, 1810 through translate and then handle, so it pins the crosswalk-to-denial mapping (1808->11 Prerequisite, 1809->12 Unavailable, 1810->13 Level). No other test checks that. It is a refusal ('changes nothing') test, so the lens requires an equally strong named replacement, and none is given.

Marked duplicate of quest_journal::breadcrumb_respects_the_quest_limit, which sends regional 10 directly. This test sends original 1811, which must translate to 14 before the Limit denial and the QuestLimit{member:true} notice. The mapping 1811->14 is unique here. The test also guards a refusal that changes nothing, so it needs a named replacement and does not have one.

Marked superseded by quest_journal::breadcrumb_for_an_active_quest_just_selects_it, which selects regional 14 directly with no translate step. This test takes original 1807 through translate for an Active quest and checks the re-press no-op. The 'done' part of the reason is not what this body tests, since the body only covers an Active quest. The cited quest_journal::breadcrumb_cannot_be_used_to_skip... test covers a completed quest, not a held one. The 1807 active-path translation is not covered elsewhere.

last_critiques.notes: I opened tests/quest_journal.rs lines 300-460. Its breadcrumb tests (crumb(id) with regional ids 10, 14, 15) call the journal directly and never call translate(), so none of them drives the original-id path that this file's start() helper exercises. The engine-level behaviour is similar, but the crosswalk mapping is not. Every removal verdict here (tests[6], [8], [9], [10]) rests on that false equivalence, and the refusal tests lack a named replacement. The keep verdicts on tests[0]-[5] and [7] look reasonable. The whole-file verdict of false is correct. Recommended: keep all five journal tests, or rewrite the verdicts to say the path is not duplicated. The reviewer's confidence of 0.6 is about right.

problems.issue: Marked superseded by quest_journal::breadcrumb_makes_the_normal_offer_and_never_completes_anything, but that test calls crumb(10) with the regional id directly and never goes through the crosswalk. The 1807->10 translate step and the giver map built in start() are only exercised here, so the offer-after-translate path has no other coverage. The auditor says as much in its own reason. A removal is not backed.
problems.fix: keep it (or first add a quest_journal or gateway test that translates original 1807 and asserts the offer, then remove).

problems.issue: Marked duplicate of quest_journal::breadcrumb_refusals_leave_state_untouched. That test covers the same 11/12/13 denials, no-change and no-award checks on regional ids. This test is the only one that proves the shipped-style originals 1808/1809/1810 translate to 11/12/13 and get the matching denial. The auditor concedes the translate step is only checked here. This is a refusal test, so the rule requires an equally strong named replacement, and none covers the translation.
problems.fix: keep it, or move the translate-to-denial mapping into a named replacement before removing.

problems.issue: Covered by quest_journal::breadcrumb_respects_the_quest_limit_and_sends_the_limit_notice, which I read in full. It asserts the Limit denial, no offer, unchanged state and the QuestLimit{member:true} notice. It does not assert no-award explicitly, but unchanged state covers that. The removal is backed, but only because the replacement checks the same thing.
problems.fix: remove is acceptable on this evidence (the auditor's moderate-confidence caveat is now resolved).

problems.issue: The quest_journal::breadcrumb_for_an_active_quest_just_selects_it covers selection, no award and no offer. The repeat-press no-change assertion (the last block, which requires !outcome.changed and an identical state) is not in any quest_journal test. breadcrumb_replayed_burst re-selects but never asserts state is unchanged. The done half is covered by breadcrumb_cannot_be_used_to_skip... The idempotence check is the part being removed and nothing replaces it.
problems.fix: keep it, or move the repeat-press no-change assertion into quest_journal::breadcrumb_for_an_active_quest_just_selects_it before removing.

last_critiques.notes: Verdicts on tests 1-6 and 8 are fine as keeps. The auditor's whole_file_removable=false is correct. The auditor's own notes say to keep the translate checks, yet its removal list still marks tests 7 and 9 for deletion, so the list is not safe to hand to a builder. The file should be kept as is, or only test 9 and test 11's repeat-press check moved after the replacements above are added.

The file's fixture builds a synthetic opening actor (patch_opening_interact_actor) and synthetic quests, so these tests are not redundant with the shipped-content tests. I did not read the npc_interaction test body in full; the superseded verdict rests on its name and the captured-frame comment. Not checked: whether the 26/10 select builder assertion is covered elsewhere.

problems.issue: The superseded verdict for interaction_request_builders_match_the_client_constructors holds, but the stated coverage is overstated. The covering test tests/npc_interaction.rs::npc_interact_26_8_decodes_and_reencodes_captured_request (line 365) does drive production decode_npc_interact_26_8 and encode() on the same 13-byte captured 26/8 frame, with truncation and invalid-bool refusals, so the 26/8 half is genuinely covered and at least as strong. The 26/10 half is not: interact_and_select_26_8_26_10_still_route (line 1229) checks routing and the malformed-selection refusal, but never asserts the 26/10 byte layout (family/subtype, GUID dwords, i32 choice at offset 12). The removed test's 26/10 assertion only checks its own file-local select_packet helper, so it exercises no production code either, and removing it loses no production check.
problems.fix: keep it removed only if the builder confirms the 26/10 layout is not a production-visible contract; otherwise keep it. Correct the reason to say the 26/10 layout is checked by no production test, so the removal rests on the helper being test-local, not on npc_interaction covering 26/10.

last_critiques.notes: Keep verdicts for tests 2-6 are reasonable: each names a distinct refusal, win-only credit, wrong-job refusal, busy-activity refusal or forged-input canary path, and none of the cited near-duplicates asserts the same outcome. whole_file_removable=false is correct. The auditor's confidence of 0.7 is fair. The single removal is defensible because the removed assertions touch no production code and the production 26/8 path is covered at least as strongly, but the reason text should not claim 26/10 coverage.

tests.name: every_enabled_quest_is_bound_to_its_giver_row_or_a_named_union_control
tests.reason: Only static cross-reference gate for the enabled quest catalogue vs. NPC giver rows. It checks loader giver/enabled agreement per record, rejects listed ids with no authored record, rejects rows that name a different giver, rejects a quest repeated inside one field, requires every enabled quest to have exactly one giver row (or be a named union control that must stay unbound), and pins the control set as enabled. tests/enabled_quest_menu_offers.rs::every_enabled_quest_is_offered_by_its_own_giver exercises offers through packets for the enabled set, but it does not assert the row-level rules (wrong-giver rows, duplicate listings, unbound-control rule, missing definitions). tests/npc_greetings_enabled_quests.rs::every_enabled_quest_giver_and_talk_target_is_bound_or_explained checks greeting strings and spawn, not quest-row binding. Refusal-style and canary-like checks, so kept under the conservative rule.

answer.notes: The file has one test, a data-consistency gate with a printed summary line. Its overlap with enabled_quest_menu_offers.rs (offer per giver, behavioural) and npc_greetings_enabled_quests.rs (greeting per giver/talk target) is partial: each covers a different assertion. Its UNBOUND_UNION_CONTROLS rule is tied to tests/scavenger_hunt_quest.rs (pins Jacque's and Ricky Danger's rows empty), which I did not open, so that cross-reference is unverified. Not verified: whether the 372 disabled-listing count is still accurate on the current tree (reported only, not asserted). Did not read enabled_quest_reachability.rs in full.

last_critiques.notes: The audit's only verdict is keep for the single test, and whole_file_removable is false, so no removal needs a covering replacement. The lens therefore has no removal to back, and the keep verdict is the conservative outcome. I checked the one cross-reference the test's doc relies on: tests/scavenger_hunt_quest.rs does pin Jacque's row (9500000497) and Ricky Danger's row to an empty quest_ids_given (around lines 1095 and 1137), and it discusses the union rule, so the UNBOUND_UNION_CONTROLS justification holds. The auditor's notes say this cross-reference was unverified; it is now verified. I did not re-read enabled_quest_menu_offers.rs or npc_greetings_enabled_quests.rs in full, so the claim that they do not assert row-level binding rules is taken from the audit's summaries. Minor: the 372 disabled-listing count is reported, not asserted, and may drift; that is acceptable under a report-only design.

answer.notes: No test in this file is a clear duplicate or obsolete. The overlap is partial: the truncation loop in test 1 repeats transport_fuzz::t1, and the bundle-depth/count checks overlap transport_fuzz::t2. last_critiques.notes: All four tests are verdicted keep, so no removal needs backing and whole_file_removable=false is correct. The cited covering tests exist at the named locations: transport_fuzz.rs t1 (line 55) and t2 (line 301), gateway.rs group_child_lengths_follow_the_client_variable_length (444) and time_response_uses_current_seconds_and_original_packet_shape (473), and login.rs group_child_lengths_follow_the_client_variable_length (1000). I did not open the bodies of the covering tests, so the partial-overlap claims are unverified. That does not affect the verdicts because nothing is removed. The optional suggestion to trim the truncation loop in test 1 is not a removal verdict. If a builder acts on it, the truncation loop must first be confirmed against transport_fuzz t1 lines 59-64. Test 1 should keep its response-byte and crc_length assertions, which transport_fuzz does not make.

problems.issue: client_direction_cannot_change_authoritative_state is marked duplicate of soccer_review::client_direction_never_scores_or_moves_authoritative_state, but the covering test is weaker on this path. The removed test's 'before' tuple also checks game.possession() and sends a vec_player_state() ClientToServer frame; the covering test checks only phase, score, clock and ball_position and sends controls and player_pos. It never sends a client PlayerState frame and never asserts possession. The auditor's own note calls the player_state vector a 'minor extra', but it is a refusal ('changes nothing') check, which the lens says needs an equally strong replacement. The covering test also uses running_match() rather than match_session(), so the fixtures are not the same. Removing this test would lose the client PlayerState no-mutation check and the possession no-change check.
problems.fix: keep it (or move the test to a removal list only after soccer_review::client_direction_never_scores_or_moves_authoritative_state is extended to send vec_player_state() and assert possession() unchanged, then re-check)

The lens's removal-backing check therefore has nothing to fail. The keep verdicts are conservative: the portal Play route, the quit and disconnect paths, the F121 canary, the F226 claim and scene-id regressions, the refusal tests and the L012 persistence and reconnect tests are each argued as reaching a boundary the similar files (soccer_service.rs, soccer_match.rs) do not reach. answer.notes: I read only lines 1-120 of soccer_service.rs and 1-550 of soccer_match.rs, so the verdicts are based on test names, doc lines and the excerpt, plus the bodies of the first 30 or so tests. The file tests the soccer_match authority module directly, and most of its tests are the only unit-level check of their behaviour. The closest overlaps are at service level: soccer_service.rs::read_only_client_packets_are_refused_with_their_actual_reason, malformed_and_non_finite_client_actions_leave_the_match_unchanged, client_owned_score_goal_and_reward_authority_is_refused, snapshot_restore_seam_preserves_the_authority_and_refuses_a_stale_save, and soccer_review.rs::client_direction_never_scores_or_moves_authoritative_state. None is a strict superset, so I kept all tests. A deeper pass would compare assertions with soccer_service.rs and soccer_review.rs for the refusal tests. No obsolete tests were found; the F1-F6 repair history reads as current policy.

problems.issue: All 28 tests are marked keep, so there are no removal verdicts to back. The lens check on superseded, duplicate or obsolete verdicts therefore has nothing to fail. whole_file_removable is false, which is consistent with keep-all.

Several keep reasons rest on unverified claims such as 'Not found elsewhere in this form' or 'Unique in the pack'. The auditor read only soccer_service.rs lines 1-120 and soccer_match.rs lines 1-550, so these claims are not checked. They do not change the outcome, because keeping is the safe direction, but the coverage claims are weak evidence.
problems.fix: keep it. Optionally re-verify the 'unique' claims against soccer_service.rs and soccer_review.rs before any future removal pass.

last_critiques.notes: The audit removes nothing, so no removal is unbacked and the file can be handed over as keep-all. The auditor was candid about its low confidence (0.4) and partial reading. Its security, refusal, persistence and canary keeps are the right default. The score is 7 rather than higher because the audit shows little verification and the coverage claims are unchecked. The id check was empty and the cross-notes were empty, so nothing contradicts the verdicts.

answer.notes: Every test here is a native-wire, refusal or canary check, so none is clearly removable. The strongest overlap is with tests/soccer.rs (synthetic_envelopes_round_trip_byte_exact, ball_transform_controls_and_player_packets_decode) and tests/soccer_match.rs (client_intent refusals for ImpulseBall and controls). Those overlaps are partial, since the other files do not assert these exact field values, so all verdicts stay keep. I did not read soccer_match.rs or soccer_service.rs in full, so a stronger duplicate could exist there; sub14_kick_state_refuses and sub13_impulse_round_trips are the best candidates to recheck against those files.

last_critiques.notes: All eight tests in tests/soccer_native_wire.rs are verdict 'keep' with covered_by null, and whole_file_removable is false. No removal, supersession, duplicate or obsolete verdict was issued, so no covering test had to be verified and nothing that is the sole check of a behaviour is at risk. The keep verdicts are the conservative choice under this lens. The removal list is empty, so it can be handed to a builder as-is. Minor weakness: the audit admits it did not read soccer_match.rs or soccer_service.rs in full, so its 'no equally strong test found' claims for the refusal tests (sub14_kick_state, sub13_impulse, malformed vectors) are unverified. That affects only the strength of the keep reasoning, not any removal, and a later audit could check those files before any removal is considered.

Same name as several other files, but the path differs (a bind refusal, not a failing event), so it is not a duplicate.

answer.notes: Every test is kept. Overlaps found: (1) inside this file, the post-settle section of a_finished_soccer_match_advances_the_quest_once repeats much of a_duplicate_settle_or_close_does_not_replay; (2) the loss and quit half of a_loss_or_cancel_does_not_advance overlaps tests/soccer_star_chapter.rs::a_loss_or_quit_does_not_credit_the_quest. Trimming either overlap would be a judgement call, not a clear removal, so I did not mark them. I did not read the helper module support/soccer_play.rs or the other files' bodies in full; the verdicts rest on the test bodies here and the names and bodies of the similar tests I checked.

last_critiques.notes: All nine tests carry a keep verdict and whole_file_removable is false, so no removal is proposed and no removal needs a covering test. The keep verdicts are safe: the refusal, security, persistence and canary tests (a_loss_or_cancel_does_not_advance, the_event_is_not_client_reported, the_credit_survives_a_reconnect, a_duplicate_settle_or_close_does_not_replay) are kept, which is the conservative direction. The auditor's overlap notes (the post-settle section of a_finished_soccer_match_advances_the_quest_once against a_duplicate_settle_or_close_does_not_replay, and the loss/quit half of a_loss_or_cancel_does_not_advance against tests/soccer_star_chapter.rs) are correctly flagged as judgement calls and not acted on. Weak points, none blocking: the 'not seen elsewhere' claims for the_reward_is_paid_once_and_the_result_precedes_the_event and a_different_game_id_does_not_advance rest on the auditor's search and were not re-verified here; the same-name a_failing_quest_event_for_one_player_does_not_stop_the_other exists in several files, and the auditor's distinction (bind refusal vs failing event) is plausible but unchecked. Confidence 0.6 is appropriate. A future pass that trims overlaps should open soccer_star_chapter.rs and support/soccer_play.rs first.

answer.notes: Net: one duplicate (client_direction_never_scores_or_moves_authoritative_state, which soccer.rs::client_direction_cannot_change_authoritative_state covers with the same assertions), eight keeps. The synthetic round-trip test is superseded for its byte-exact part by soccer.rs::synthetic_envelopes_round_trip_byte_exact (all_vectors() includes vec_player_pos), but its decoded-flag assertion is unique, so it is kept. Not verified: whether soccer_match.rs or soccer_native_wire.rs contain decode-refusal or restart-gating tests that would supersede parts of the mixed tests (possession_chain_and_decode..., restart_and_end...). Those would be the next thing to check before trimming. Since the file's refusal checks are unique, it should not be removed as a whole.

problems.issue: Marked superseded by soccer.rs::synthetic_envelopes_round_trip_byte_exact, but the auditor admits it did not check this against soccer.rs:453. I read that test: it loops over all_vectors() and asserts encode(decode(bytes)) == bytes. That is a real byte-exact round trip, so the encode/decode path is covered. The review test also has an explicit assertion that decode(player_pos()).flag is false, and the covering test never checks the decoded flag. A byte-exact round trip would catch a flag that was dropped on encode, but not one that was decoded wrongly and then re-encoded consistently. The auditor's note calls this a minor add-on, but the lens asks for an equally strong replacement, and none is named. It is also unconfirmed whether all_vectors() includes the player-position vector at all.
problems.fix: Keep the test, or split off only the flag-0 decode assertion into a named guard and confirm all_vectors() includes the UpdatePlayerPos vector before removing the rest.

problems.issue: Duplicate verdict checks out. soccer.rs::client_direction_cannot_change_authoritative_state (lines 259-292) drives the same path. It sends player_pos, controls and player_state as ClientToServer and asserts phase, score, clock, possession and ball position are unchanged. It also refuses a client goal, keeps the score at [0,0], and accepts a server goal. The review test's extra assertions are minor.
problems.fix: Remove is supported. Name soccer.rs::client_direction_cannot_change_authoritative_state as the replacement.

problems.issue: The keep verdicts are the safe direction under the lens. The covering tests named for these (for example goal_sets_scoreboard, clock accepted path, restart happy path) only cover accepted paths, so refusal and persistence checks are not replaced. The auditor did not claim any of them is removable.

last_critiques.notes: Only two removal verdicts exist. The duplicate is backed by soccer.rs:259. The superseded one is only partly backed: the round trip is covered, but the explicit flag-0 decode assertion is not, and the auditor did not verify the claim. whole_file_removable=false is correct. Other covering tests named for keep verdicts were not needed for removal.

problems.issue: client_direction_never_scores_or_moves_authoritative_state marked duplicate of tests/soccer.rs::client_direction_cannot_change_authoritative_state. Checked: soccer.rs:259-292 drives the same ClientToServer player_pos/controls/player_state vectors, asserts phase, score, clock, possession and ball_position unchanged, refuses a client goal with score [0,0], then accepts a server goal to [0,1]. The review test's assertions are a strict subset (it omits player_state and sends no player_state vector), so removal loses nothing. Backed.

Verdict keep is correct. The byte-exact round trip is covered by soccer.rs::synthetic_envelopes_round_trip_byte_exact (soccer.rs:453-458 over all_vectors()), but the decode(player_pos()).flag == false assertion is unique to this test.
problems.fix: keep it (or trim only the round-trip loop into a named guard that keeps the flag assertion)

problems.issue: Keep is safe. Refusal of non-A+B totals, non-advancing scores and replayed goals has no equivalent in soccer.rs; the auditor's claim that soccer.rs covers only the accepted path is consistent with what was read.

Mixed test. The auditor did not verify soccer_native_wire.rs for decode refusals (the file was searched for restart/GoalMade/NaN/register only, not decode truncation or flag refusals). The keep is safe, but any future trim of decode-only assertions needs that check first.
problems.fix: keep it; if trimming, split decode refusals out only after verifying soccer_native_wire.rs

problems.issue: Keep is safe; NaN/infinite/out-of-order clock refusals are not in soccer.rs. Unverified claim that no other file covers them, but keeping costs nothing.

Restart/end gating refusals are asserted as unique, but soccer_match.rs::halves_transition_and_the_finished_outcome_is_once_only was not checked. Keep is safe under the lens since the removal list is not affected.
problems.fix: keep it; verify soccer_match.rs halves test before any trim

problems.issue: Keep is safe. Slot-duplicate, reassignment and out-of-range refusals are not covered by soccer.rs, which uses team assignment only as setup.
Keep is safe. Goal-during-restart-hold refusal is distinct from soccer.rs::goal_sets_scoreboard_holds_clock_and_restarts, which never sends a goal during the hold.
Keep is safe. Non-finite ball geometry rejection is a hostile-input guard; soccer.rs has no equivalent and the auditor's search of soccer_match.rs found only player NaN tests.
Keep is safe. Unregistered-holder refusal is distinct from soccer.rs's accepted-chain test and soccer_match's proximity assignment test.

last_critiques.notes: Only one removal verdict exists (tests[6]) and it is backed by a covering test with the same path and at least the same assertions. All other verdicts are keeps, which the lens prefers when unsure. whole_file_removable=false is correct because eight tests have no equivalent. The auditor's confidence of 0.7 reflects unverified overlaps in soccer_match.rs and soccer_native_wire.rs, which affect only future trimming, not the current removal list. The stated covering test for tests[6] is the only removal in the list and the list is wireable as it stands.

answer.notes: Low-effort audit: I read only the entry-frame, join, tick, shot, pass and controls tests plus the file header and a few similar-file names, not every test body or the similar files' assertions. Every test is kept conservatively: this service file sits one layer above soccer_match (authority) and soccer_entry (zone/payout), and its wire-layout, refusal and persistence checks are not shown to be duplicated. Overlaps worth a deeper pass later: soccer_entry::forged_entries_and_client_goals_change_nothing vs client_owned_score_goal_and_reward_authority_is_refused; soccer_entry::quitting_before_a_result_cancels_without_a_payout vs disconnect_mid_match_cancels_run_and_never_pays; soccer_match::snapshot_restore_survives_reconnect_and_rejects_replays vs snapshot_restore_seam_preserves_the_authority_and_refuses_a_stale_save.

last_critiques.notes: The audit issues no removal verdicts. All 16 tests are marked keep and whole_file_removable is false, so the lens's requirement that every removal be backed by a named replacement is vacuously met. Keeping a redundant test is the safe direction under the brief, so the list can be handed to a builder as a no-op. The score is held down because the audit is self-described as low effort (confidence 0.5). Several keep reasons say 'not verified' or 'not clearly covered' without opening the comparison tests, so the audit does not establish that the overlapping pairs are distinct. (2) The test is #[ignore] and needs a local capture, so it does not run in default CI. That is a coverage-visibility issue to note for the lead, not a reason to remove it. The doc line is empty, so intent rests on the module comment and body, as the auditor noted.

tests.name: exchanges_reference_handshake_over_loopback_udp
tests.reason: Only end-to-end check that the soe-probe binary, launched as a process, binds loopback UDP, ignores a malformed datagram, answers the synthetic session request with the exact compiled response bytes from the sender's address, and exits after one reply. tests/session.rs::shared_session_matches_compiled_fixture_and_real_client_crc_length checks the same fixture bytes only in-process via SessionRequest::parse(..).response(), with no socket, no process, and no malformed-then-valid ordering. The probe's unit tests in src/bin/soe-probe.rs cover the handshake in-process too, not the real wire path. Not clearly covered elsewhere, so keep.

answer.notes: Single test, slow-ish (spawns a process, 3s read timeout) but it is the only real-socket check of the probe binary. Overlaps in fixture bytes with tests/session.rs and tests/transport_fuzz.rs (which use the same fixtures in-process), but those do not exercise the UDP/process boundary. Probe is documented as historical in notes/Project Map.md; if the probe is retired, this file becomes obsolete together with src/bin/soe-probe.rs, not before.

last_critiques.notes: The only test, exchanges_reference_handshake_over_loopback_udp, is marked keep, and whole_file_removable is false. No removal verdict is made, so the evidence lens (superseded, duplicate or obsolete tests need a named replacement) has nothing to check against. The keep reason is sound: the test is the only one that drives the real loopback UDP and process boundary, with a malformed datagram before the valid request, the exact fixture response bytes, the sender address check, and a clean exit. The in-process session.rs and transport_fuzz.rs checks share fixture bytes but do not cover the socket path, so they do not make this test redundant. Minor point: the notes say the probe is historical. That could justify a future retirement of the probe and this file together, but it is not a removal now, so the keep stands. I did not open the cited session.rs test or the soe-probe.rs unit tests, since no removal depends on them.

last_critiques.notes: The audit removes nothing: all seven tests are marked keep, whole_file_removable is false, and no test is marked superseded, duplicate or obsolete. In tests/soe_send.rs, the RetryLimit and SenderFailed assertions appear only at lines 213-231 of that file. tests/piece_094.rs:302 checks only RetryLimit, which matches the auditor's description of it as weaker. MessageTooLarge appears once in transport_fuzz.rs:275, also as described. The stated reasons for keeping are consistent with the grep evidence. answer.notes: The file is a Harvesting111 clone of tests/type8_gateway.rs (Mining18). Several test names match one-to-one, and the shared code path is probably the generic Type8 engine. I judged each test as keep because each asserts harvesting-specific ids, strings, or content, and the pack excerpt shows no matching assertions elsewhere. Only the sibling test bodies were not read in full, so I could not confirm assertion-level equality. If a later review confirms that type8_gateway.rs drives the same generic engine path with identical assertions, the cloned tests (disabled dev tools, the wrong-profile test, and the absent-content test) become duplicate candidates. I did not read the other similar files (kart_service, forging, derby_route, kart_npc_entry); they are unrelated to this harvesting path.

last_critiques.notes: Every verdict is keep, so no removal needs a covering test and the evidence lens has nothing to reject. whole_file_removable is false, which is consistent with the keep verdicts. Keeping all 14 is the safe direction under the rule that a lost check costs more than a redundant one. The score is held down because several keep reasons rest on unverified sibling comparisons. The auditor says it did not read type8_gateway.rs bodies and states that the sibling tests assert different things (for example, release versus rebind, and different content files) without checking. Those claims could be wrong. If the sibling bodies do drive the same generic Type8 engine with the same assertions, the cloned tests (disabled_dev_tools, wrong_profile, content_absent, strings_byte_identical) would be duplicate candidates. A follow-up that reads type8_gateway.rs could turn those keeps into justified removals. It is not a blocker for this audit. Confidence 0.6 is honest.

The keep direction is the safe one under this lens. Weak spots that do not block the pass: (1) the audit read vendor_sell.rs only in the 740-1000 range and did not check the other similar files' bodies, so its claims that no other test pins the forged-price path or the 165/5 interleaving are unverified rather than checked; (2) buy_and_sell_refusals_change_nothing overlaps several vendor_sell.rs refusal tests. answer.notes: Low confidence: the pack's test bodies were truncated and the previous answer was itself cut off, so I read only parts of this file (about lines 600-884) and two overlapping coin_store_siblings tests. I did not read the service-layer refusal and coin-cap tests in full, nor the vendor-buy tests after line 884 beyond their names, so every verdict defaults to keep. Overlap is most plausible between the sell-replay and buy-back-replay tests and between the vendor routing tests in npc_interaction.rs; a full read of both files would be needed before removing anything. The file is clearly not removable as a whole: it holds the only native 165/5 sell and refusal coverage in the set.

problems.issue: The only removal, gateway_vendor_buy_debits_grants_and_replies, is marked superseded by coin_shop.rs::vendor_buy_debits_grants_and_retries_without_replaying. I read that covering test (coin_shop.rs 370-394). It calls the service method shop.buy_vendor directly and never goes through the gateway packet route, the 66/44 reply path, or the at_open_shop fixture. The gateway test's unique value is that routing: a vendor buy packet arriving through Gateway::handle_at with an open shop, then the last reply read as status 1. The covering test does not drive that path, so the removal is not backed. The auditor's own note says the covering test was not checked line by line, and the lens requires that check.
problems.fix: keep it. Remove the superseded verdict unless a named gateway-level success test for the vendor buy packet is found (for example in vendor_buy_sell_gateway.rs) and shown to assert the debit, the grant and the status 1 reply.

last_critiques.notes: The other 17 keep verdicts are safe because keeping is the cautious choice, and the auditor's covered_by claims for them are only noted as possible overlaps. I read the gateway tests at lines 700-960 and the covering test in coin_shop.rs; the gateway refusal and canary tests assert more than the coin_shop refusal test does. The 'not verified line by line' caveat on the one removal is the decisive gap. Whole-file removal is correctly rejected because the fixtures are unique to this file. With the removal reversed, the removal list is empty and can be handed over as 'keep all'. Not checked: the overlap claims for coin_store_siblings, piece_084 and npc_interaction are unverified, but they are only reasons for keeping, so that does not change the outcome.

problems.issue: The only removal, gateway_sell_replay_of_a_whole_stack_pays_once, is marked duplicate of tests/vendor_sell.rs::replay_and_reload_cannot_pay_twice. I read both. The covering test sells one item (SELLABLE_INSTANCE, 75060) at service level via Counter::send, replays it once, then replays after a save/reload. It never goes through the gateway. The removed test sends a whole-stack sell (STACK_ONE) through the gateway with gateway routing and the 165/6 wire completion, then replays it three times and asserts the completion result is RESULT_INVALID_ITEM and the inventory is unchanged. The covering test does not check that wire reply on the gateway path, so the paths differ. The auditor also admitted this is its lowest-confidence removal. Replay-no-double-payment is a security/canary invariant, so the lens requires an equally strong named replacement, and none exists.

last_critiques.notes: Every other verdict is keep, so no other removal is at risk. The auditor's own 'not read in full' caveats cover the service-layer tests (lines 238-730) and the coin_store_siblings overlaps it cites (sell_then_buy_back_once_restores_the_stack_and_the_exact_coins, buy_back_keeps_the_open_shop_and_range_checks). Those are keeps, so they are safe, but they remain unverified. The audit's 'whole_file_removable: false' is supported. The removal list is not wireable as it stands: the one removal is unbacked and should be changed to keep before the list is handed to a builder. Confidence in this critique is moderate-high, since I checked the two named tests directly but not the coin_store_siblings overlaps.

Other tests load job_abilities.json for behaviour (job_basic_attacks, opening_abilities, weapon_requirements, job_trainers), not for this ratio cross-check, and the canary is not repeated anywhere else.

answer.notes: Both tests cover reference data that no other test file validates, so nothing is redundant. The file is small (141 lines, two tests, no crate modules or shared helpers). The agent notes in notes/Autopilot/T635.md confirm the file was added with the reference build and that both tests pass. Neither test has a later task that replaced it. Confidence is lower because I only compared test names and grep results, not the full bodies of the similar files.

last_critiques.notes: Both tests are marked keep with whole_file_removable false, so no removal verdict needs a covering test. The lens checks therefore pass by default. I confirmed the audit's one checkable factual claim: a repo-wide grep for weapons.json, attacks.json and job_abilities.json shows that tests/weapon_reference.rs is the only test that reads weapons.json and attacks.json. The other hits are the build script, notes, and the loader code. job_abilities.json is loaded by several behaviour tests (ability_lookup, encounter_job_skills, job_trainers, job_ability_bars, opening_abilities, job_basic_attacks, power_up_use). I did not open their bodies to confirm none of them checks multipliers, but that only matters if this file were removed, and it is not. Minor gap: the audit's 'similar files' argument was based on names and scores, not bodies. It does not change the keep verdicts.

answer.notes: Only a truncated excerpt of the file's first half was in the pack, so I read the full file myself. I did not read opening_abilities.rs beyond its test names, so the per-slot weapon_class check in the last test was not compared against it. Three of the four tests are #[ignore]d and need external packages or a live gateway, so they do not run in the default suite. The one test that can cheaply be trimmed is the basic-row half of shipped_combat_rows_require_each_jobs_weapon_class. The whole file is not removable.

problems.issue: The verdict is keep, but the reason suggests dropping the basic-row half of shipped_combat_rows_require_each_jobs_weapon_class in a cleanup. The per-slot skill half is not verified as covered: opening_abilities.rs:540 mentions weapon_class, and the auditor did not read that file, so the per-slot half is not established as unique.
problems.fix: keep it. If a cleanup is later done, drop only the basic-row loop (lines 405-412) after confirming opening_abilities.rs:540 does not already cover the per-slot check. Do not treat this as a removal in the current list.

last_critiques.notes: Every verdict is keep and whole_file_removable is false, so no removal is made on the auditor's authority and the lens's removal-backing requirement is not triggered. The keep reasons were checked against the repo: the wrong-class and unequip-revocation assertions in the first test are unique at unit level, and the three #[ignore]d tests are the only ones that exercise the wand/gateway path and the no-weapon refusals on every route. answer.notes: No test here is a clear duplicate or superseded: the quest ids 3000320-3000323 and 3000360 appear in no other test file, and the file is the only one that runs these chains. Several test names (progress_survives_reconnect, xp_goes_to_adventurer_with_another_job_active, two_players_are_independent, early_*_refused) repeat across zone_quests_wilds/sanctuary/merry_vale/wugachug_briarwood. Those share a template but drive different quests, so they are not duplicates. I could not open the sibling files (only the excerpt and names were reachable), so cross-file comparison rests on names and the pack. Possible cleanup: fold feminine_touch_completes into the xp test, or strengthen the xp test to assert Adventurer XP. Neither is a removal.

last_critiques.notes: All eight tests are marked keep with covered_by null, and whole_file_removable is false. The lens checks removal verdicts, and there are none, so nothing needs a named replacement. Keeping every test is the conservative direction and the auditor's verdicts are consistent with the evidence pack. The removal list is empty, so it can be handed to a builder as is. Residual weaknesses, none of which justify a removal: (1) xp_goes_to_adventurer_with_another_job_active asserts only that Miner XP is unchanged and not that Adventurer gains XP, so its name overstates it; strengthening it is a follow-up, not a removal. (2) The claims that 3000320-3000323 and 3000360 appear in no other test file, and that the same-named tests in the wilds, sanctuary, merry_vale and wugachug files drive different quests, were not verified against those files. They only matter if a future pass proposes removing a same-named test. (3) feminine_touch_completes could be folded into the xp test, but folding is not removal and the auditor already kept it.

tests.name: accepting_at_the_gate_rank_completes_at_once
tests.reason: Checked job_level_quest.rs::accepting_at_level_five_completes_immediately (lines 401-415): it only asserts counts [1], unchanged profile XP and objective_complete on accept. It does not run the Talk, the 49/13 end screen, the coin payment, the 49/14 settle or the Completed status, which this test does. So it is not the same path and is not superseded. Keep.

answer.notes: Every test checks a distinct path for quest 3130017, which no other file drives end to end. The prior superseded verdict on accepting_at_the_gate_rank_completes_at_once was wrong because its cover stops before the turn-in and payment, as the critique said. The shared overlap with job_level_quest.rs is the job_level objective mechanism only, on a different quest and reward. No duplicates or obsolete tests found. Judged from the excerpt and the cited cover test, not from a full suite run.

problems.issue: The superseded verdict for accepting_at_the_gate_rank_completes_at_once is not backed. The named cover, job_level_quest.rs::accepting_at_level_five_completes_immediately (lines 401-415), only accepts at rank 5 and asserts counts == [1], profile XP unchanged, and objective_complete. It never runs the Talk, the 49/13 end screen, the 49/14 settle, the coin payment, or the Completed status. The removed test does all of those, and turn_in() asserts pending turn-in, end-screen reward, coin credit and no job XP, then Completed. So the cover is a partial path, not the same path. The auditor's own reason concedes the Completed check is the only extra, but turn_in's payment assertions are also absent from the cover. Postman accept-then-pay at the gate rank is then tested nowhere else in this file or in job_level_quest.rs for quest 3130017. Keep it, or re-cite a cover that includes the turn-in and single payment.

last_critiques.notes: The four keep verdicts are reasonable. Each is a refusal, persistence or the main end-to-end path for quest 3130017, which the auditor says only this file exercises. The W5 file covers the same mechanism for a different quest, so it does not replace them. The only removal candidate is the accept-at-rank test, and its cover does not assert payment or completion status. whole_file_removable is false, which is correct. Confidence 0.6 is honest, but the removal should not be wired as it stands. Full suites were not run; the judgement rests on reading the cover test and the excerpt.

All five tests are marked keep, so no removal verdict needs a covering test. The keep direction is the safe one, and nothing here would delete a sole check of a behaviour. whole_file_removable is false, which is consistent with the keep verdicts. The cross notes and the automatic id check are both empty. The only shortfall is in the justifications: the claims that no other file covers the short-of-gate refusal, the another-job refusal and the reconnect path for quest 3130017 were not checked against the suite. That affects only the strength of the keep reasons, not the verdicts. The accepting_at_the_gate test correctly records that job_level_quest.rs::accepting_at_level_five_completes_immediately stops before the turn-in and payment, so it is not superseded. The file is ready to hand over as a keep-all list.

tests.name: encode_lays_out_the_native_reader_field_order
tests.reason: Only byte-level layout check of opcode 31 in this crate; the reader order is the wire contract. Other files (housing_service.rs ~L1485, world.rs) compare encoded output only against their own fixtures, not the field offsets.

tests.name: decode_round_trips_the_documented_fields
tests.reason: Only decode-side check of the documented field set against the captured field map. Partially overlaps the encode test, but it is the sole decode-to-struct assertion for this codec.

tests.name: utf8_names_use_byte_length_and_round_trip
tests.reason: Pins that the length prefix is a byte count for non-ASCII names; no other test in the pack checks this.

tests.name: decode_refuses_wrong_envelope_opcode_and_length
tests.reason: Refusal check (wrong family, opcode, short/long length, empty and truncated input). Must be kept.

tests.name: bounded_string_reads_refuse_oversize_overrun_and_negative_lengths
tests.reason: Hostile-input refusal check on string length prefixes. Must be kept.

tests.name: non_finite_floats_are_refused_on_both_paths
tests.reason: Refusal check for NaN/inf on encode and decode. Must be kept.

tests.name: booleans_decode_as_nonzero_and_encode_canonically
tests.reason: Pins the non-canonical boolean decode policy and canonical re-encode; unique to this codec.

tests.name: short_tails_trailing_bytes_and_oversize_strings_are_refused
tests.reason: Refusal check for short tail, trailing bytes and oversize encode input. Must be kept.

tests.name: defaults_do_not_invent_flags_or_geometry
tests.reason: Checks defaults produce no flags or geometry; cheap and not clearly covered elsewhere. Conservative keep.

tests.name: captured_op31_frame_round_trips_byte_exact
tests.reason: Ignored, env-gated byte-exact canary against the preserved capture (SHA-256 pinned). Not run by default; keep as a canary.

answer.notes: The file tests the codec directly and no other file in the pack or the src/zone_transition.rs module (no inline tests found) asserts the same field offsets, refusals, or boolean policy. Housing and world tests only compare encoded output against their own fixtures, which is not the same assertion, so nothing was marked superseded or duplicate. Similar-file scores (housing_native, npc_interaction, kart_lobby_native) are for different codecs. Confidence is moderate because I did not read the similar files' assertions in full; the housing_service.rs encode-equality check at ~L1485 is the closest overlap and is weaker than this file's field-level checks.

last_critiques.notes: The audit proposes no removals. All 10 tests are marked keep and whole_file_removable is false, so no removal verdict needs a covering test, and nothing that is the sole check of a refusal, persistence, security or canary behaviour is at risk. The keeps are conservative. The stated reasons for 'no other test covers this' are only partly verified: the auditor says it did not read the similar files' assertions in full, and it cites housing_service.rs ~L1485, which is not in the evidence pack's most-similar list. That weakens the confidence figure (0.8) but does not change any verdict, since nothing is removed. If a later pass proposes removing any of these tests, the claim that housing_native.rs and world.rs only compare against their own fixtures would need to be checked first.
